## Prepare an independent review

Under **Prepare a complete migration review**, choose:

| Selection | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Original source | The complete publisher document being migrated or accepted. |
| Preceding catalogue edition | An optional, separately retained document used to inspect changes across publisher editions. |
| Candidate source | The original converter or preserved 3.0 source by default; select another received document when reviewing an operator correction. |
| Normalize a flat DCAT-US 3.0 catalogue | An explicit request for the original 3.0 normalization. Leave it off for the default preserved-source review. |
| Review label | A useful name for this exact selection and review. |
| Explicit identity changes | Optional verified mappings for deliberately changed dataset or series identifiers. |

Choose **Prepare migration review**. Each preparation records a new saved
review with its own source, comparison, candidate and review identities.
Preparing a correction leaves the earlier review available in **Saved review**.

The engine converts a selected 1.1 catalogue through the original converter.
An already 3.0 document follows its corresponding preserved-source review by
default. To request the original normalization of a flat 3.0 catalogue, select
**Normalize a flat DCAT-US 3.0 catalogue** and prepare a separate review. The
review retains this explicit selection and every resulting change. A supplied
operator-corrected candidate follows its own review of the retained bytes.
The returned conversion state, messages and original exception explain the
actual result. The source, candidate and comparison each have their own
validation result.

A conversion that cannot produce a candidate still becomes a saved review with
its original error and validation results. **Download complete review** and the
original-source download remain available. Receive a corrected complete document
and prepare another review to continue; candidate download, identity mapping
against that candidate, and cutover become available when candidate bytes exist.

For a source-only review:

~~~sh
starforge dcat review \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source RECEIVED_SOURCE_ID
~~~

For a following edition with a retained predecessor:

~~~sh
starforge dcat review \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source FOLLOWING_SOURCE_ID \
  --comparison PRECEDING_SOURCE_ID
~~~

Use the saved review ID returned by the operation. The complete original
engine report carries a **review_sha256** binding its selected inputs and
result.


For explicit 3.0 normalization:

~~~sh
starforge dcat review \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source RECEIVED_3_0_SOURCE_ID \
  --normalize-v3 true
~~~

The default is false. Inspect the returned **normalize_3_0** or
**preserve_3_0** mode with the complete validation and field changes.
Changing this choice changes the automatic candidate, so identity-mapping drafts
remain bound to the original source, candidate and normalization selection.

## Read the review in a useful order

### Overview

Overview shows the saved review, original conversion result, issues, declared
source identities and candidate identity. It retains the full engine report
behind **Complete original engine report**.

The source and candidate SHA-256 values identify different artifacts whenever
conversion or correction changes the bytes. Candidate origin records whether
the engine converted the source, preserved it, or reviewed an operator-selected
candidate. The source label and declared origin remain visible beside those
identities.

**Engine review SHA-256** binds the engine's reviewed result. The saved review's
**reviewSha256** and **summary.reviewSha256** both contain that same intrinsic
**review_sha256**. **Saved report file SHA-256**, retained as **reportSha256**,
identifies the complete downloaded report bytes. Check downloads against the
file hash; use the intrinsic review hash when recording a release decision.
The browser retains original numeric values, including large integers and long
decimals, throughout report display and typed identifier mapping. New reviews
identify their exact decimal comparison as **numeric_comparison: exact-decimal.v1**.
They compare the values from the retained source and candidate independently of
the unchanged GSA converter. If conversion rounds a decimal value, its before
and after values appear as a field change for the original record. Existing
saved reviews keep their original report bytes, hashes and release associations;
prepare a new review of the same retained sources to obtain the corrected comparison.
Catalogue, review and release lists show local dates; complete saved identities
and downloaded files retain their exact recorded timestamps.

The engine's **can_receive** result controls candidate selection. If the
candidate needs correction, use its validation and conservation results to
prepare that correction and run a new review. A review that is ready for
receiving still needs an operator's actual cutover decision.

### Validation

Read **Original source validation**, **Candidate validation**, and, when
selected, **Preceding edition validation** separately.

Each result retains the original schema ID, validator state, record results and
exception. The view shows actual checked, valid and invalid record counts.
Catalogue, individual-record and nested-catalogue errors share one searchable
issue browser; equivalent path/rule/message occurrences are grouped while their
original schema paths and contexts remain available. Every reported error includes its document path, schema path,
validator name, message and full context. The interface filters by path or
message and by validation rule. It pages through the complete retained error
array, 25 issues at a time.

A path points into the original document associated with that result. Correct
the selected candidate's actual value or structure, then receive that complete
candidate and create a new review. Preserve the source report so the operator
can explain the correction later.

### Record conservation

**Record conservation** shows how each dataset or dataset series travels from
the source to the candidate. Its counts include source records, candidate
records, matched identities, missing identities and added identities.

Open the complete identity mappings to inspect:

- Source and target record pointers.
- Original and target identifiers.
- Dataset or series roles and catalogue locations.
- Whether the engine matched the original identity or used an explicit mapping.
- Relocation and changed-field information.

Missing records, added records, duplicate identities and unidentified records
remain visible with their original descriptors. Duplicate and unidentified
results keep their source and candidate sides separate.

**Review converted fields** filters the complete records by identifier, field
path, record type and change type. Every row retains its source and candidate
paths, classification and complete values. Expand a record to inspect its
fields. The view pages through records without removing them from the saved
report.

The value display distinguishes an absent property, JSON null, an empty
string, arrays and nested objects. These values can carry different meaning in
a catalogue. Review the actual change and the converter's classification before
making a correction.

### Successive editions

This section keeps publisher-edition changes separate from conversion changes.
It provides two views when the comparison is available:

| Comparison | Left-hand document | Right-hand document |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original source and preceding edition | The selected source being reviewed | Its separately supplied preceding catalogue edition |
| Reviewed candidate and preceding edition | The candidate from this review | That same preceding catalogue edition |

The labels follow the original engine's comparison direction. **Only in
source** and **Only in comparison** refer to those exact sides. Use the retained
identifiers and source dates when deciding whether the publisher added,
removed or changed a dataset over time.

Each view retains full conservation, field changes and catalogue-level changes.
Filter by an actual identifier or nested field path to inspect, for example,
publisher, licence, access-rights or distribution changes without losing the
complete other records. Download the full report when a receiving operator
needs every comparison value in one file.

## Correct a candidate without losing its history

When the saved review contains a candidate, use **Download candidate** to obtain
its exact bytes and keep that file. Make the intended correction in another
complete JSON document. If the original conversion failed before producing a
candidate, keep its complete review and original source, and prepare the
corrected full document from that source and its reported conversion errors.

Receive the corrected document through the same upload form:

1. Give the correction its own label and source reference.
2. Choose its declared profile.
3. Select **Operator-corrected candidate** as its intended use.
4. Complete receiving.
5. Keep the original publisher document selected as **Original source**.
6. Select the new received document as **Candidate source**.
7. Keep the same predecessor when that comparison remains relevant.
8. Add only the explicit identity mappings needed for intended identifier
   changes.
9. Prepare a new review and inspect its validation, conservation and field
   changes.

The source, original converter output, corrected candidate and each review
remain separately addressable. A later operator can reconstruct what changed
and why.

### Deliberately change an identifier

The mapping editor has four fields for each intended identity change:

| Field | Required original value |
| --- | --- |
| source_path | Exact JSON pointer of the source record. |
| target_path | Exact JSON pointer of the candidate record. |
| source_identifier | Identifier actually present at the source pointer. |
| target_identifier | Identifier actually present at the target pointer. |

Select actual source and candidate records from a conservation review that
matches the current source and candidate selection, or enter their exact values.
Prepare a candidate-producing review or select a separately received corrected
candidate before adding mappings. A draft remains associated with its selected
source, candidate and normalization mode; return to that selection or use **Clear draft mappings**
before entering mappings for different documents. Identifier fields accept JSON: a plain
identifier is a quoted JSON string, while a structured Identifier retains its
complete object, including every original property. The field editor displays
an @id or notation label when available and retains the full typed value.
Record-pointer fields remain exact text JSON pointers.

The engine verifies the selected paths and values. A mapping records intended
identity continuity while preserving the original identifiers and locations.

For a CLI review, save the actual mappings as a JSON array in a private file:

~~~json
[
  {
    "source_path": "/dataset/0",
    "target_path": "/dataset/0",
    "source_identifier": "the-actual-original-identifier",
    "target_identifier": "the-actual-corrected-identifier"
  }
]
~~~

The illustrative values above must be replaced with the original document's
values. Then run the same review selection:

~~~sh
starforge dcat review \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source RECEIVED_SOURCE_ID \
  --comparison PRECEDING_SOURCE_ID \
  --candidate CORRECTED_CANDIDATE_ID \
  --mappings /absolute/private/source/identity-mappings.json
~~~

An ordinary field correction that preserves identity uses the same corrected
candidate flow with no mapping file.

## Select the reviewed catalogue release

Open **Cutover & rollback** on the exact saved review.

Read the current selected release and the candidate's receiving result. Record
the operator, reviewed exceptions, intended scope and cutover decision in the
note. Choose **Select this reviewed candidate**.

The workspace requires the expected current active-release ID. Its first

browser also supplies the selected review's intrinsic **reviewSha256** and

workspace and review the current release before saving the next decision.

A completed cutover creates an immutable release entry containing the review,
preceding release, candidate SHA-256, time and operator note. Its reviewed
candidate becomes the active downloadable catalogue.

The equivalent first selection is:

~~~sh
starforge dcat cutover \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --review REVIEW_ID \
  --expected-active none \
  --review-sha256 ENGINE_REVIEW_SHA256 \
  --candidate-sha256 CANDIDATE_FILE_SHA256 \
  --note "Operator and actual reviewed cutover decision"
~~~

For a following cutover, replace **none** with the actual active release ID
returned by the current project. Supply the selected saved review's actual
**reviewSha256** and **candidateSha256** for the optional CLI hash flags shown
above, and preserve the returned release and candidate identities.

The browser's active-release download is bound to that saved release's review.
The authenticated **/api/dcat/current/download** endpoint serves the workspace's
currently active catalogue. Complete release history keeps the preceding
candidate accessible for restoration.

### Apply the release to the customer's catalogue service

Use the saved candidate's exact bytes as the input to the customer's existing
catalogue deployment process. The useful handover sequence is:

1. Retain the currently deployed catalogue artifact and the deployment
   configuration needed to restore it.
2. Download the selected review's exact candidate and keep its SHA-256 and
   release identity.
3. Apply that candidate through the existing catalogue service's normal
   deployment path.
4. Read the deployed catalogue back through its ordinary public or authenticated
   endpoint and compare it with the selected candidate and service behavior.
5. Record the deployed URL, deployment operation, operator and actual result
   with the customer handover.

The workspace selection and customer deployment have separate operating
identities. Keeping them together in the handover makes the selected release
and its actual service deployment easy to follow.

## Restore a prior release

Choose the prior release in **Restore a prior catalogue release**. Record the
operator and rollback reason, then choose **Restore selected prior release**.

The operation checks the expected active-release ID and creates a new history
entry selecting the prior candidate. It retains the release being replaced and
its original review. The complete history links each review and allows the
operator to open it directly.

The CLI uses the same original saved releases:

~~~sh
starforge dcat rollback \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --release PRIOR_RELEASE_ID \
  --expected-active CURRENT_RELEASE_ID \
  --review-sha256 PRIOR_RELEASE_REVIEW_SHA256 \
  --candidate-sha256 PRIOR_RELEASE_CANDIDATE_SHA256 \
  --note "Operator and actual rollback reason"
~~~

For the restored target, use that historical release's **reviewSha256** and
**sha256** as the review and candidate hashes. Its ID and hashes identify the
selected prior artifact; **expectedActiveReleaseId** identifies the current
release being replaced.

After restoring the workspace selection, apply the selected prior artifact
through the customer's deployment process. Verify that the service is serving
the intended prior catalogue and keep that deployment result with the rollback
entry.

## Export the review and complete workspace

The review's download controls provide the original source, candidate, complete
report, predecessor and operator-candidate original when present.

Use the same saved review through the CLI:

~~~sh
starforge dcat export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --review REVIEW_ID \
  --kind candidate \
  --out /absolute/private/delivery/catalogue-candidate.json

starforge dcat export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --review REVIEW_ID \
  --kind report \
  --out /absolute/private/delivery/catalogue-review.json
~~~

For a complete handover, choose **Open complete workspace handover** in the
migration section. The existing **Workspace** section creates the original
whole-project archive, including the DCAT documents, reviews and release
history with the project's other retained operations.

Follow the current workspace operation to completion before exporting. Keep
the returned archive, exact byte count, SHA-256 and manifest identity. The
native CLI follows the same archive engine:

~~~sh
starforge dcat archive \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --out /absolute/private/delivery/catalogue-project.ckanw
~~~

Include these original materials with a customer delivery:

| Material | What the next operator receives |
| --- | --- |
| Installed application package, manifest and source revision | Editable application and its original dependency selection. |
| Prepared migration runtime | The selected Python executable and pinned converter/schema dependencies. |
| Complete .ckanw archive and its SHA-256 | Original catalogue documents, reviews, corrected candidates, active selection and complete release history. |
| Selected candidate and complete review | A directly usable catalogue artifact and its full source/conversion/comparison record. |
| Deployment and rollback instructions | The customer's actual service entrypoint, retained prior artifact and deployment operation. |
| Operator decisions | The scope, exceptions, cutover and rollback rationale already associated with the saved releases. |

## Receive and reopen as the next operator

Receive the exact archive into a new private destination:

~~~sh

  --file /absolute/private/delivery/catalogue-project.ckanw \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-catalogue-project

starforge dcat serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-catalogue-project
~~~

Use the archive's complete SHA-256 from its actual export. The receiver
continues the original archive operation for the same archive and destination.
It preserves the saved source, review and release identities while relocating
the project through the existing whole-workspace receiver.

In the reopened browser, inspect the active release, open its review, download
its candidate and inspect the preceding release. Continue with a following
publisher edition or an intended correction in this same project. The complete
earlier history remains available for the next cutover or restoration.

The existing [workspace operating guide](../../../../products/ckan/OPERATING.md)
describes the surrounding capture, publication, merchant and buyer workflows.
Use them when the customer's project also includes retained CKAN resources and
native data products.

## Operate through the merchant agent

The DCAT tools use the existing merchant CKAN workspace alias and lease. Select
the same initialized catalogue project in the host's private configuration.
Declare original catalogue documents as **dcat-catalog** input aliases and, when
needed, a complete mapping JSON file as a **dcat-mappings** alias. Use
**merchant_ckan_inputs** to inspect their actual file identities.

| Tool | Saved-project operation |
| --- | --- |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_status | Read the current operation and retained catalogue, review and release inventories through their original pages. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_import | Receive an input alias with its expected SHA-256, label, profile and origin. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_review_prepare | Prepare a separate review of source, comparison, candidate, typed identity mappings and optional 3.0 normalization. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_review | Read a saved review's summary and all selected report sections. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_files | Select an original catalogue, report, candidate or current release file. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_file_read | Read the selected exact bytes through the original retained-file reader. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_cutover | Select the exact reviewed candidate as the active release. |
| merchant_ckan_dcat_rollback | Restore a previous candidate through another release-history entry. |

Read **merchant_ckan_status** before each mutation and supply its current
**expectedOperationId**, together with the selected **workspace** alias. Follow
the returned native operation to completion, then refresh before the next
mutation. Browser, CLI and agent retain the same catalogue, review and release
IDs.

Import uses **input** for the declared alias and **expectedSha256** for its
selected complete file. Optional **profile**, **label** and **origin** describe
that document. Review preparation uses the resulting **sourceId**, optional
**comparisonId** and **candidateId**, and **normalizeV3**. Supply either complete
typed **identityMappings** or the original **mappingsInput** alias and
**expectedMappingsSha256**. Keep structured identifiers as their complete JSON
objects and string identifiers as strings.

The review summary returns **reviewId**, intrinsic **reviewSha256**, **status**,
**report**, and **summary.sections**. Section pages retain **section**, **edition**,
**rows** and **page**. Each row carries its exact **reportPath**, **value** and
optional **owner**. Continue **page.nextOffset** until it is null; keep the same
review and section selection. An oversized row is explicitly identified and
remains available in the complete raw report. Corrections-needed reviews remain
saved results: receive the corrected document separately and prepare a new
review.

File selection takes **kind** as **catalog**, **report**, **candidate** or
**current**, with **itemId** except for current. The result's **file** contains
the stable kind/itemId, name, byte count, SHA-256 and original **read** arguments.
A current-release request resolves to the actual retained candidate before
reading. Use the returned **expectedSha256**, then retain **readId** and
**nextOffset** for the subsequent **offset**/**limit** reads. Assemble the bytes
in order, verify the complete file hash and release the reader through
**merchant_ckan_file_release**. The report file hash is distinct from its
intrinsic review hash. These byte reads preserve catalogue encoding and any
byte-order mark.

Cutover takes **reviewId**; rollback takes the selected historical **releaseId**.
Both require the current **expectedActiveReleaseId** (UUID or null), exact
**expectedReviewSha256**, **expectedCandidateSha256** and the operator's **note**.
For cutover, use the saved review's intrinsic **reviewSha256** and
**candidateSha256**. For rollback, use the target release's **reviewSha256** and
**sha256**. Refresh the current active release before recording either decision.

Complete handover continues through the existing
**merchant_ckan_workspace_archive**, **merchant_ckan_workspace_inspect**,
**merchant_ckan_workspace_read** and **merchant_ckan_workspace_receive** tools.
Keep the complete archive hash, receive into the declared new target alias, and
reopen that same received project. These tools retain the original archive and
relocation engine used by Workspace and **starforge dcat**.

# Install the catalog workspace with Python 3.12

The catalog workspace can use an explicitly selected Python 3.12 runtime while retaining the complete original GSA converter, schemas, dependency lock and review behavior. Use the `portable-python312` profile for that interpreter. The default `original` profile follows the upstream Python requirement, `>=3.13,<4.0`, and is installed through [DCAT_ENGINE.md](DCAT_ENGINE.md).

This guide applies to the source directory containing this file. In the installed `ckan-merchant` package, it is `source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/`. The source checkout has the same path without the leading `source/`. Keep the application source read-only and place its Python environment and saved customer workspaces in separate owned directories.

## Install the complete original dependency selection

Select an actual Python 3.12 executable. From this guide's directory, create a private environment at an absolute path of your choice:

~~~sh
umask 077
python3.12 -m venv /absolute/private/dcat-python312
/absolute/private/dcat-python312/bin/python -m pip install \
  --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: \
  -r portable-runtime-requirements.txt
/absolute/private/dcat-python312/bin/python -m pip check
/absolute/private/dcat-python312/bin/python -B dcat_migration.py \
  --runtime-profile portable-python312 --check-runtime
~~~

[portable-runtime-requirements.txt](portable-runtime-requirements.txt) is the complete export of the original lock's 47 main packages, pinned to their original versions and all 679 original distribution SHA-256 hashes. The lock itself remains unchanged at [vendor/gsa-dcat-us/jsonschema/poetry.lock](vendor/gsa-dcat-us/jsonschema/poetry.lock). Its SHA-256 is `20318bd0c8a2213346f0acce36c639c2f3da8162b18e08641bf347e3df1349b1`; the requirements export is `1cef430eb3989ca9faab7120341d651343014706707e77cd43ad50ecad7af33c`.

For an existing wheelhouse that carries this exact lock selection for the host's Python ABI and platform, add `--no-index --find-links /absolute/wheelhouse` to the install command. Hash checking remains enabled. A missing compatible wheel means that wheelhouse needs the actual locked distribution before installation can finish.

The engine verifies its original source files and registry selection before importing the converter. The runtime output records the real interpreter, installed dependency versions, matches to the retained lock and required format checkers. Preserve this output with the customer installation record. The IRI checker is part of the required original dependency selection; it determines whether a proposed series identity satisfies the actual schema.

The portable profile accepts Python `>=3.12,<3.13`. Setting a Python executable alone keeps the default `original` profile. Choose both the executable and profile when starting the maintained application.

## Start the command line and browser application

Set the two host environment values for the installed `starforge` command:

~~~sh
export SCF_DCAT_PYTHON=/absolute/private/dcat-python312/bin/python
export SCF_DCAT_RUNTIME_PROFILE=portable-python312
starforge dcat init --workspace /absolute/private/customer-catalog \
  --origin https://catalog.example/
starforge dcat serve --workspace /absolute/private/customer-catalog --port 0
~~~

Use the private application URL returned by the running process. A saved project can be reopened with the same `serve` command. The Node application selects the configured executable with shell execution disabled; customer catalog JSON cannot set the runtime profile.

Use the installed Node runtime required by the package. Exact-number catalog and mapping handling uses Node 22.16 or newer and its original JSON source-token support. [MIGRATION_OPERATING.md](MIGRATION_OPERATING.md) covers the complete browser and command line workflow, including comparison, typed corrections, normalization, review, cutover, rollback and full workspace receiving.

For a first source review, retain the original full editions and import them separately:

~~~sh
starforge dcat import --workspace /absolute/private/customer-catalog \
  --file /absolute/catalogs/legacy-data.json --profile 1.1 --label "Original legacy edition"
starforge dcat import --workspace /absolute/private/customer-catalog \
  --file /absolute/catalogs/current-data.json --profile 3.0 --label "Published comparison edition"
~~~

Each import returns the saved catalog identity. Select those exact identities in the browser, or pass them as `--source` and `--comparison` to `starforge dcat review`. The application retains the complete originals. A 3.0 source is preserved byte for byte by default; explicit normalization creates its own recorded review selection.

The engine's complete review can return status 2 when the candidate needs correction. The application saves that full review and its actual schema findings. An edited candidate and its exact typed identity mappings can then produce another review without changing the retained converter or either source edition.

Add the following values to the existing private Applications environment JSON object:

# CKAN data products

Create a retained data product from an existing CKAN DataStore, choose the fields
and customer query policy, publish the dataset, and deliver its merchant package
and buyer request through the original Stellar Forge engines.

The local interface covers catalogue discovery, capture and resume, edition
comparison, field selection, candidate preview, review, version publication,
merchant packaging, release staging and buyer preparation. It uses a restrained
industrial layout with explicit forms and the real retained project state.

## Start a project

Use Linux with Node 24 or newer and util-linux `flock`. Archive downloads use the
system `tar` command. Run these commands from the SCF source directory:

```sh
mkdir -m 700 ./ckan-work

node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs init \
  --project ./ckan-work/library \
  --origin https://ckan0.cf.opendata.inter.prod-toronto.ca

node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs serve \
  --project ./ckan-work/library --port 8457
```

Open the printed project link. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 and the link carries
the project capability in its fragment. The browser removes the fragment from its
address bar and retains the capability for this session. Project API requests use
an authorization header and verify the local host and origin.

The installed distribution exposes `starforge ckan` and the original
publisher adapter as `starforge ckan-publisher`. Invoke the installed command
using the same options. `ckan help` lists each native action.

For a catalogue that requires an existing API token, pass its environment variable
name with `init --auth-token-env CKAN_TOKEN`. The project records that reference.
Provide its value in the serving/capture process environment.

## Operator workflow

1. **Find and retain an edition.** Search the catalogue and open an advertised
   DataStore resource. Choose source filters, query, pagination and capacity.
   Capture saves the original package/resource responses and every accepted page.
   After a process interruption, open the same project and resume the edition.
2. **Review the source fields.** Open a complete edition to see the actual rows,
   provider types, null/empty counts and suggested aliases. Select the fields,
   scalar types and explicit conversion for the product. Compare an earlier
   edition of the same resource by a unique source key when available.
3. **Prepare the queryable product.** Select equality filters, range fields,
   sort fields, extraction ordering and customer page sizes. The original
   durable publisher creates the typed CSV, dataset configuration and candidate.
   Preview actual customer queries through the original dataset engine.
4. **Record the review and publish.** The review binds the displayed candidate
   digest and original version target. Publish initializes the dataset version.
   Recovery reads the original publication outcome after an interrupted response.
5. **Package and stage the merchant.** Enter public payment terms and the
   intended resource address. Download the complete portable package or stage it
   in the project's original SF82 release store. The original seller console owns
   activation, process start/stop, comparison and rollback.
6. **Prepare the buyer request.** Read the running seller's actual offer for the
   selected edition and query. Choose its payment alternative and intent ID,
   then download the original SF88 configuration.

Each mutation records its result in the project. A project has one active
operation at a time and one kernel-owned workspace lock. Close the serving process
before using another process to mutate the same project.

## Capture and import from the CLI

The original Toronto source selection is included in
[examples/toronto-library-selection.json](examples/toronto-library-selection.json).

```sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs capture \
  --selection sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/examples/toronto-library-selection.json \
  --out ./ckan-work/toronto-capture

node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs import \
  --project ./ckan-work/library \
  --capture ./ckan-work/toronto-capture/capture.json
```

Re-running `capture` with the same selection and directory resumes the retained
pages. A complete capture is reused only when its original selection matches.
Use a new directory to acquire a fresh edition. `import` copies and verifies the
complete retained edition; an already imported manifest resolves to its existing
project entry.

For a complete acquisition already retained by Commons' connected public-source
helper, use `capture-received`. The [receiving guide](RETAINED_PUBLIC_SOURCE.md)
covers original response bundles, interrupted receiving and integration with the
same import and reviewed refresh workflow.

`captureSelection()` accepts the canonical HTTPS catalogue origin, package and
resource IDs, explicit filters, optional full-text query, page size and pagination.
Offset pagination is the default. CKAN 2.12 keyset pagination uses the returned
`next_page` filter; selections with an existing `_id` filter use offset mode.

The capture follows the provider's returned `limit`, checks exact totals, and
retains estimated-total status. Duplicate record IDs, changed field declarations
and inconsistent terminal pages produce a retained error with the edition still
available for inspection. Provider HTTP 429 retains its response receipt and
retry guidance for a later resume.

Successful capture metadata includes the observation interval, original source
selection, page requests and digests, original license fields, and resource
metadata before and after paging. Its observation kind is
`sequential-datastore-pages`. This makes the acquisition method and any
resource metadata change visible when an edition is reviewed.

## Field types and exact values

A saved source uses `stellar-forge.ckan-source.v1` and named projection queries.
Each customer alias selects one original CKAN field and an explicit type:

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `native` | Retain a compatible string, safe integer, finite number or boolean. |
| `text` | Convert a reviewed scalar into text; exact numeric tokens retain their original value. |
| `json` | Retain structured values, scalar JSON types and exact numeric tokens as JSON text. |
| `nullable` | Permit source null for the selected scalar column. |

Aliases use the original dataset identifier rules. Suggested names are
deterministic and avoid collisions. The source field remains in the declaration,
so labels such as `Service Tier` can be exposed as `service_tier` without losing
their original field identity.

The original CSV engine represents an empty nullable cell as null. Use JSON text
when one field contains both actual empty strings and nulls. Exact numbers that
JavaScript would round, overflow or underflow are retained using the original JSON
token and require text or JSON projection. Ordinary compatible numbers remain
typed. Browser samples display exact values as text to preserve what the operator
reviews.

The [Toronto projection example](examples/toronto-library-projection.json)
shows seven useful fields and their actual nullability. The corresponding
customer policy can expose equality filters on `physical_branch` and
`service_tier`, and sorting on `branch`. Original query syntax includes
`where_physical_branch=1&sort=branch&limit=50`.

# Recurring catalogue acquisition and accepted editions

Use the existing **Catalogue migration** workspace to receive a publisher's
current DCAT-US document, retain its complete source and HTTP history, and
review the next edition against an explicitly selected accepted release.
Source configuration, acquired documents, conversion reports, operator
corrections and release history travel together in the complete workspace.

This is the following-edition workflow in the original DCAT application.
The source acquisition keeps publisher documents; the migration engine makes
the review; the existing release operation selects the accepted candidate.
Each step keeps its original identity so another operator can reopen the
whole project and continue it.

## Open the installed workspace

Install and open the project using [Migration operation](MIGRATION_OPERATING.md).
Use **DCAT catalog migration** in the original Applications console, or:

~~~sh
starforge dcat serve --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project
~~~

Use the same configured Python runtime as the existing migration project.
[DCAT_ENGINE.md](DCAT_ENGINE.md) describes the original runtime, and
[PORTABLE_RUNTIME.md](PORTABLE_RUNTIME.md) describes the explicitly selected
portable profile. Acquisition and review use the same saved workspace and
operation owner as uploads, corrections, cutover and rollback.

## Add the original publisher source

In **Catalogue migration → Recurring catalogue sources**, choose **Add source**.
Enter a useful label, the publisher's document URL and its declared profile:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Original publication URL | The actual document to retrieve, for example the publisher's complete data.json. |
| Document profile | auto detects the retained document; 1.1 and 3.0 are explicit declarations checked by the existing engine. |
| Private token environment name | Optional name of a token already configured in the private application environment. Save its name in the source. |
| Check interval | Whole minutes from 1 to 525,600; default 60. It determines when a source is due. |
| Request timeout | Whole milliseconds from 100 to 300,000; default 30,000. |
| Maximum response bytes | Whole bytes from 1,024 to 134,217,728; default 134,217,728. |
| Include this source in due checks | Enabled by default. Clear it to pause scheduled due selection while preserving manual acquisition. |

For a public example, the official
[data.gov GSA JSON record](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/gsa-json)
identifies [https://gsa.gov/data.json](https://gsa.gov/data.json) as GSA's
published catalogue source. Acquire its actual current document. Its contents,
record counts and HTTP result are recorded when the operation runs.

Save the source and follow the original workspace operation. A newly allocated
source identity stays selected while its save finishes. Its saved source
configuration includes a sourceSha256, version history and the latest acquired
catalogue binding. The browser keeps the original draft available when an
unsuccessful save has not replaced it.

To change a source, choose **Edit selected source**. The editor binds the
configuration SHA inspected when it opened. If another operator changed that
configuration, retain the draft and reopen the current source before saving.
An actual configuration change starts a new version and clears that version's
current catalogue and conditional-request binding. Acquire the new version
before preparing a source review. All prior configuration versions, HTTP
attempts, documents and reviews remain retained.

The private token belongs in the same host or private Applications environment
used to launch the saved project. The browser accepts an environment-variable
name, not a token value. A receiving operator supplies that environment on the
destination host; the saved source retains the reference.

## Acquire and inspect the current document

Choose **Acquire current source edition**. The request binds both the current
sourceSha256 and expectedLatestCatalogId, including null before the first
document. Follow the shared operation progress above the migration view.

Public-source acquisition uses the retained HTTP conditional-request information
when it applies to the same source configuration. Credential-referenced sources
receive complete HTTP entities on each check, so a changed private credential
cannot inherit a previous credential's conditional result. **Request the current
document without conditional cache headers** explicitly requests a fresh
response. Every request still respects the retained publisher retry time.

Inspect the original acquisition history:

| Outcome | Operator continuation |
| --- | --- |
| FETCHING | Follow the active operation until the saved attempt completes. |
| ACQUIRED | A downloaded edition is retained and selected as the source's latest catalogue. Review it before cutover. |
| UNCHANGED | The received bytes match the retained catalogue. Inspect the original attempt and keep the linked catalogue. |
| NOT_MODIFIED | The publisher returned a conditional unchanged response linked to a verified retained catalogue. |
| FAILED | Inspect the saved error, HTTP receipt and any retained response; correct the cause and retry when allowed. |
| INTERRUPTED | Inspect the retained attempt and continue with its retry identity after the current operation has ended. |

The table shows started and completed times, HTTP status, response byte count
and completeness, the linked catalogue and the complete saved attempt.
Search by URL, attempt identity, catalogue or error; filter by outcome and page
through the complete history. **HTTP receipt** downloads the original request
and response history. **Original response** downloads its exact saved bytes.
A partial body is labeled **Retained incomplete response** and stays distinct
from a received catalogue.

The source shows lastCheckedAt, nextCheckAt and retryNotBefore. A Retry-After
response remains part of the source and attempt history. Acquisition and retry
controls are unavailable until that time; refresh the workspace when due.
For an unsuccessful attempt under the same configuration, **Retry this
acquisition** records retryOf rather than concealing the previous attempt.
Changing the source configuration preserves the old attempt and uses the new
configuration's own acquisition history.

**Download source configuration and history** includes the selected source,
all of its retained acquisitions and its saved review descriptors. The original
HTTP receipt and response files remain separately downloadable.

## Review against an accepted predecessor

The source panel reviews its latest acquired document. Its label, received
time and SHA-256 stay visible. Older documents remain available through the
ordinary retained catalogue and migration review controls below.

1. Choose an **Accepted predecessor release**, or explicitly leave
   **No accepted predecessor** for an initial review.
2. Read the selected release and its original review. **Open accepted
   predecessor review** displays that saved report; its candidate download
   retains the exact previously accepted bytes.
3. If that accepted report contains explicit identity mappings, select the
   decisions to carry into this edition. The complete typed identifiers and
   original JSON pointers are shown for each decision. The list is searchable
   and paged; selection uses each original zero-based mapping index.
4. If you have corrected the newly received document, upload that complete
   edited candidate through **Receive catalogue** and select it explicitly in
   **This edition's corrected candidate**. Otherwise the automatic candidate
   comes from the current acquired source.
5. Leave 3.0 normalization unchecked to preserve an already-3.0 document.
   Select it only for the existing explicit flat-3.0 normalization operation.
6. Choose **Prepare source edition review**, then follow the original
   operation. Its allocated review opens in the existing complete viewer.

The browser binds the accepted release's candidate SHA-256 and intrinsic
review SHA-256. Its mapping choices come from that release's complete
report.identity_mappings. With an automatic candidate, selected accepted
identifier decisions apply to the newly converted current source while its
other fresh fields remain intact. With an explicitly uploaded corrected
candidate, the engine preserves its bytes and resolves each selected decision
against the current source and candidate by exact typed identifier, catalog
scope and record role. Record paths may have moved. Missing or ambiguous
identities, overlapping choices and stale baseline hashes require a corrected
selection. Each review retains the newly resolved exact mapping pairs.

**Additional explicit identity mappings** accepts an optional JSON array for
this edition. Each row uses source_path, target_path, source_identifier and
target_identifier. Preserve actual typed JSON values: a string identifier
stays a string, and a structured identifier keeps its complete object. The
ordinary review viewer can build mappings from actual retained record rows.
Its exact JSON reader and writer preserve numeric tokens used in the source.

Changing the source version or latest catalogue opens a separate review
selection draft for that edition. Changing the accepted predecessor clears
the previous baseline's selected mapping indexes. **Download this review
selection** retains the chosen source, baseline and explicit decisions for the
operator's working record.

## Resolve findings and select the release

The prepared review uses the original GSA conversion and schema validation,
record conservation, full field changes, catalogue changes and successive
edition comparisons. Read all validation scopes and the complete source and
candidate identities. A corrections-needed review remains saved and readable;
a failed conversion can retain a full report without candidate bytes.

Correct an edited candidate or explicit identity mapping using
[MIGRATION_OPERATING.md](MIGRATION_OPERATING.md), then prepare a separate review.
The original acquisition, prior report and prior release remain inspectable.
A successful acquisition alone does not change the active release.

Use the existing **Select reviewed catalogue** operation after inspecting the
complete accepted candidate. It checks expectedActiveReleaseId and the selected
review/candidate hashes and records an immutable release. Download that exact
candidate for the customer's catalogue deployment process and record the actual
deployment context in the release note.

For rollback, choose the original historical release in the existing release
panel, inspect its original review and candidate hashes, and record the reason.
Rollback creates a new history entry selecting the prior candidate. It does not
remove the following acquisition, review or release. The selected active
catalogue is available through **Download active candidate** and the original
current-download endpoint.

## Run due checks through the existing scheduler

The saved interval supplies due information. The browser does not create a
background scheduler. Use the host's existing scheduled operation and the
original owner of the saved project.

### While the browser or managed application is running

Start the original server with a private startup record outside the portable
project:

~~~sh
starforge dcat serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --startup-file /absolute/private/launch/catalogue-startup.json
~~~

The startup file's directory must belong to the operator and allow access only
to that owner. The record contains the original bearer URL; keep it in private
host configuration. The same original startup record may be selected from the
existing managed application's private output.

Invoke due checks through that running owner:

~~~sh
starforge dcat acquire-due \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --startup-file /absolute/private/launch/catalogue-startup.json
~~~

The client verifies the original authenticated /api/launch instance, process
and project binding, dispatches only sources actually due through that server,
and follows each retained acquisition ID. A busy owner defers the check to the
next existing host invocation, preserving the operator's in-progress work.
The source interval and retained publisher retry limit remain effective.

### When the workspace is closed

The command can acquire the existing project lease itself:

~~~sh
starforge dcat acquire-due \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project
~~~

Use this form only when the browser or managed application is not holding the
project. It selects enabled sources whose next-check and retained retry limits
allow a request and follows each original acquisition operation.

Pausing a source excludes it from due checks; its source and earlier editions
remain available, and an operator can still explicitly acquire it. A newly
configured or changed source is independently acquired and reviewed before a
new release is selected.

## Installed command workflow

Use the actual IDs and hashes returned by the saved project:

~~~sh
starforge dcat save-source \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --label "GSA published catalogue" \
  --url https://gsa.gov/data.json \
  --profile auto \
  --interval-minutes 60

starforge dcat status --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project
starforge dcat source --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project --source SOURCE_ID

starforge dcat acquire \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source SOURCE_ID \
  --expected-source SOURCE_SHA256 \
  --expected-latest none
~~~

For a later acquisition, replace none with the inspected current catalogue ID.
To request the document without conditional headers, add --unconditional true.
To preserve an unsuccessful attempt's relationship, add --retry-of ACQUISITION_ID.

Updating a source requires --source and --expected-source together. The
required --label and --url state the complete current selection. Omitted
--profile and --token-env preserve those existing fields. Use
--token-env NAME to select a configured private environment variable;
--token-env none clears its reference. Set --enabled false to pause due checks.

Prepare the following-edition review with an accepted predecessor:

~~~sh
starforge dcat review-source \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --source SOURCE_ID \
  --expected-source SOURCE_SHA256 \
  --expected-latest LATEST_CATALOG_ID \
  --baseline-release ACCEPTED_RELEASE_ID \
  --baseline-sha256 ACCEPTED_CANDIDATE_SHA256 \
  --baseline-review-sha256 ACCEPTED_REVIEW_SHA256 \
  --reuse-mappings 0,2 \
  --label "Following publisher edition"
~~~

Select only indexes actually present in the inspected accepted report.
Omit --reuse-mappings when carrying no prior decisions. Omit the three baseline
arguments for an initial review. Optional --candidate CATALOG_ID selects an
independently uploaded edited candidate; --mappings /absolute/decisions.json
supplies the exact typed mapping array; --normalize-v3 true selects explicit
normalization.

Download the original acquisition files:

~~~sh
starforge dcat export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --kind receipt --acquisition ACQUISITION_ID \
  --out /absolute/private/delivery/http-receipt.json

starforge dcat export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/catalogue-project \
  --kind response --acquisition ACQUISITION_ID \
  --out /absolute/private/delivery/original-response.bin
~~~

The existing inspect, cutover, rollback and original/candidate/report/current
export commands continue unchanged. Keep the intrinsic reviewSha256 distinct
from the SHA-256 of the full retained report file.

Choose **Open complete workspace handover** in Catalogue migration. Workspace

# Receive a retained public-source acquisition

Use `capture-received` when the original CKAN responses have already been acquired
through Commons' connected public-source helper. It consumes the complete bundle
locally and produces a normal CKAN capture for import, semantic projection,
merchant publication and reviewed refresh.

The receiving command invokes `captureCkanResource()` from this directory.
The existing engine parses the literal source bodies, follows the selected
pagination, checks the provider's exact totals and field declarations, preserves
exact numeric tokens, and compares source metadata before and after paging.

## Acquire and retain the complete source

The acquisition carrier is Commons
[`host/connected_public_source.cjs`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/commons/blob/main/host/connected_public_source.cjs).
Keep the literal acquisition result and its complete `commons.source-bundle/v1`
JSON file with the original operation ID. Its receipt identifies every original
public HTTPS URL, successful upload/download, response byte count, digest and
acquisition time.

Acquire these named members in order for the exact selected resource:

| Member | Original response |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | `package_show` for the selected package |
| `resource.json` | `resource_show` before paging |
| `schema.json` | Selected CSVW schema, when configured |
| `pages/00000000.json`, and following numbered pages | Each original `datastore_search` response through its terminal page |
| `resource-after.json` | Independent `resource_show` after paging |
| `schema-after.json` | Independent following CSVW schema, when configured |
| `public-source-receipt.json` | Complete acquisition receipt, included by the helper |

The DataStore URL must be the exact request generated by the selection: resource
ID, limit, `sort=_id asc`, records format, total flag, filters, optional query
and offset or keyset cursor. Preserve each literal JSON body. A selected page
size is a request; pagination completion follows the returned page limit and
total through the original engine.

The helper's JSON members use `encoding: "base64"` and the `content` field.
The receiver validates each decoded member against its declared bytes and
SHA-256. It also binds the successful carrier receipt to those same source
members, upload IDs, download IDs and original URLs.

## Receive, import and refresh

Place the complete bundle and selection in a private directory. Use the original
bundle's exact byte count and SHA-256; receiving is a local operation.

```sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs capture-received \
  --bundle ./ckan-work/source/source-bundle.json \
  --bytes BUNDLE_BYTE_COUNT \
  --sha256 BUNDLE_SHA256 \
  --operation ORIGINAL_OPERATION_ID \
  --selection ./ckan-work/source/selection.json \
  --out ./ckan-work/received-capture

node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs import \
  --project ./ckan-work/library \
  --capture ./ckan-work/received-capture/capture.json
```

The command prints the real capture path and manifest SHA-256, complete manifest,
and acquisition binding. The existing workbench accepts this capture through
`import`. Follow [REVIEWED_REFRESH.md](REVIEWED_REFRESH.md) to compare an
existing published source with the following edition, review its actual changes
and publish the accepted successor.

Programmatic callers import `receivePublicSourceCapture` from
`retained-public-source.mjs`. The first argument has the same six named
inputs as the CLI: `bundleFile`, `bundleBytes`, `bundleSha256`,
`operationId`, `selection` and `captureDirectory`. The optional
second argument passes the original capture capacity, cancellation and
`onProgress` callback. The receiving transport always reads the selected
bundle.

## Continue an interrupted run

Re-run with the same bundle identity, operation, selection and capture directory.
The receiving path binds these inputs before capture. The original capture lock
and progress journal own the operation.

On resume, the receiver checks actual saved response files before constructing
the remaining source sequence. This covers a process stopping between saving a
response body and updating capture progress. A completed capture is reused after
its full retained body hashes and selection are checked. Existing raw responses
require the original capture progress.

The capture directory contains:

- The normal `capture.json`, `progress.json`, original metadata and numbered pages.
- `source-input.json`, binding this capture to the bundle and selection.
- `source-acquisition.json`, the literal original acquisition receipt.
- `source-acquisition-binding.json`, binding the completed native capture
  hash and row/page counts to that receipt.

Keep these companions and the complete source bundle in the delivery alongside
the native capture and any resulting merchant workspace. Companion paths are
relative to their capture directory, so separate editions remain independent.

## Metadata and resource limits

The connected import returns the complete body and its successful transfer
receipt. It omits upstream HTTP response status and headers. Native capture
receipts therefore retain `status: null` and empty HTTP headers; the
acquisition receipt retains the original connector metadata and source times.
The native capture's receiving clock describes local consumption of those saved
responses.

This path accepts public sources on the selected HTTPS catalogue origin.
Credential-bearing selections continue through the ordinary direct capture
route. The original capture limits remain in force. The complete source bundle
has a 96 MiB receiving limit and up to 256 acquired members, matching the
connected source helper's maximum source count.

# Review a complete CKAN refresh

The publisher can retain a complete comparison between two original captured
editions, review its source terms and field meanings, and publish an accepted
successor. Every decision stays attached to the exact saved comparison. The
previous publication remains available through its original publication ID,
dataset snapshot and merchant package.

The same workbench owns the browser, CLI and merchant MCP operations. Its
existing Linux project lease serializes all changes. Workspace archives include
the comparison files, decisions, selected successor and earlier publications.

## Operator workflow

1. Open the existing project and choose **Reviewed refresh**.
2. Select the original saved source and its published predecessor. Capture the
   following selection through the original catalogue engine, or select an
   already complete retained edition.
3. Choose one or more source key fields. Prepare the full comparison and inspect
   its source selection, terms, definitions, row totals and change pages.
4. Review the successor's public aliases and types. The field editor preserves
   existing aliases, shows missing prior fields, and leaves new fields
   unselected until chosen. Preview validates every retained after-row and
   returns the exact projected semantic dictionary.
5. Enter the operator name and a source/change review note, then record one
   decision.

| Decision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Accept | Creates a distinct saved source with the reviewed projection and semantic identities. Continue through the original candidate preparation, review and publication workflow. The new publication records its predecessor and exact refresh decision. |
| Keep current | Retains the original source and its published versions. The complete reviewed comparison and decision remain available. |
| Withdraw source | Ends future candidate preparation, candidate review and publication from that selected source. Existing published versions remain readable; a separately accepted successor remains usable. |

The page offers the full JSONL download and comparison/decision records. Each
change retains its key, complete before/after values and changed field names.
The existing quick edition comparison remains a 100-change preview; **Reviewed
refresh** retains every change.

A completed decision is immutable. **Start a new review of these editions**
links another explicit decision to the prior review. This lets an operator
reconsider the same original editions while ordinary repeated preparation
continues to reuse its original comparison and successor identity.

## Interpret source windows correctly

The comparison records the catalogue, package, resource, filters, query and
schema URL for both original captures. A changed date window or filter is shown
as a changed selection. Added and removed rows describe membership in those
retained selections; inspect the recorded interpretation before treating a
difference as a provider deletion or update.

Page size and pagination configuration are retained separately from the
membership selection. Source metadata changes contain the original package
and resource fields, including terms, descriptions and identifiers. Field
meaning changes use the original retained CSVW/definition engine.

Keys contain one to sixteen distinct source fields. Every selected key must be
present, non-null and unique in each capture, with scalar values. Composite
keys preserve their field order and value types. Numeric keys and row values
use the original exact CKAN number parser. Decimal spellings are compared
mathematically without JavaScript integer rounding; signed zero remains
distinct. Strings remain strings, and an absent field remains different from
a field containing null.

The full JSONL retains original numeric tokens. Browser and MCP JSON
presentations show exact numeric tokens as text so a downstream JavaScript
JSON parser cannot round them.

## CLI

All commands operate on the same private project directory:

    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-prepare --project PROJECT --id SOURCE_ID --input refresh.json
    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID
    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-preview --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID --input projection.json
    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-changes --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID --sha256 COMPARISON_SHA256 --offset 0 --limit 50
    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-file --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID --sha256 COMPARISON_SHA256
    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-review --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID --input decision.json

The preparation input selects the actual saved source and after-edition:

    {
      "afterEditionId": "ACTUAL_EDITION_UUID",
      "expectedSourceSha256": "ACTUAL_SAVED_SOURCE_SHA256",
      "expectedAfterCaptureSha256": "ACTUAL_CAPTURE_SHA256",
      "previousPublicationId": "ACTUAL_PUBLISHED_PREDECESSOR_UUID",
      "keys": ["_id"]
    }

The preview input includes the returned exact comparison SHA-256. Omit
projection/query/title to inspect the original selection on the following
edition; supply them to review a changed public projection.

    {
      "expectedComparisonSha256": "ACTUAL_COMPARISON_SHA256"
    }

For accept, copy the actual preview's normalized projection and query, its
projection SHA-256, and both nullable semantic identities into the decision:

    {
      "expectedComparisonSha256": "ACTUAL_COMPARISON_SHA256",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reviewer": "Operator name",
      "note": "Describe the source, terms, selection and field-meaning review.",
      "expectedProjectionSha256": "ACTUAL_PREVIEW_PROJECTION_SHA256",
      "expectedSemanticsSha256": "ACTUAL_PREVIEW_SEMANTIC_SHA256_OR_NULL",
      "expectedDefinitionSha256": "ACTUAL_PREVIEW_DEFINITION_SHA256_OR_NULL"
    }

The last two values are explicit JSON null when the original preview has no
semantic review. When editing aliases or query, also include the exact
previewed projection/query/title. For keep-current or withdraw-source, those
successor projection fields are unnecessary.

The returned acceptedSourceId continues through the existing commands:

    node ckan/cli.mjs prepare --project PROJECT --id ACCEPTED_SOURCE_ID --input publication.json
    node ckan/cli.mjs inspect --project PROJECT --id PUBLICATION_ID
    node ckan/cli.mjs review --project PROJECT --id PUBLICATION_ID --input candidate-review.json
    node ckan/cli.mjs publish --project PROJECT --id PUBLICATION_ID --review-id REVIEW_ID

Use the original candidate digest and review ID returned by those steps.
The refresh decision selects source data and meaning; the original publisher
still reviews its complete candidate and creates the dataset version.

## Agent tools

The managed merchant host registers forty CKAN tools, including these seven
reviewed-refresh operations:

| Tool | Original operation |
| --- | --- |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_prepare | Prepare or recover the exact comparison from source and after-edition identities. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh | Read full comparison metadata, source/meaning differences, preview and saved decision. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_resume | Continue the original comparison or finish its already saved decision. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_preview | Validate all after-rows and return the exact successor projection and dictionary identities. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_changes | Page retained changes with the returned nextOffset. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_read | Read the entire unchanged JSONL in SHA-256-pinned native chunks. |
| merchant_ckan_refresh_review | Save accept, keep-current or withdraw-source on the selected comparison. |

Each changing tool requires the current expectedOperationId, including explicit
null when the original project has no operation. Follow that returned original
operation to completion before the following mutation. Read tools operate on
the same owner. The normal file_release tool closes an abandoned chunk read.

For refresh_read, supply expectedComparisonSha256 and expectedSha256 from
comparison.changes.sha256. Continue with its readId and nextOffset until
nextOffset is null. The full change file uses the existing read-only retained
file reader; the browser download streams the same bytes with
x-content-sha256.

The native comparison page API accepts up to 200 requested rows; MCP accepts up
to 100. A four MiB presentation budget can shorten either response. Always use
nextOffset. An individual record exceeding that page budget returns
CKAN_REFRESH_CHANGE_REQUIRES_DOWNLOAD; its complete record remains in the
original JSONL download.

## Interruption and complete receiving

Each comparison directory contains input.json, the original append progress,
changes.jsonl, its sparse changes.idx and comparison.json. The comparison pins
both captures and complete output files. The index addresses every 128th change
and supports direct later-page reads.

A resumed build checks its saved prefixes and original inputs before
continuing. Completed comparisons retain their exact bytes. A decision is
saved before source creation; accepted source IDs are allocated during the
original preparation. If the process ends after decision storage, resume
finishes that same decision and source rather than issuing another one:

    node ckan/cli.mjs refresh-resume --project PROJECT --id REFRESH_ID

The original whole-workspace archive includes refreshes with all retained
capture, publication, merchant and buyer history:

    node ckan/cli.mjs archive-workspace --project PROJECT --out COMPLETE.ckanw
    node ckan/cli.mjs inspect-workspace --archive COMPLETE.ckanw --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256
    node ckan/cli.mjs receive-workspace --archive COMPLETE.ckanw --project NEW_PRIVATE_PROJECT --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256

Receiving rebinds original source locations while preserving comparison and
decision bytes. It checks comparison/capture/source relationships, accepted
projection/semantic identities and original publication history. Earlier
archives without refresh records remain supported. The existing browser and
five agent workspace-transfer tools carry the same complete workspace.

## Run the complete real-source receiving example

examples/reviewed_refresh.mjs continues a specific published project using its
actual retained data. Supply exact original IDs and either an original complete
capture.json or a live capture selection JSON:

    node ckan/examples/reviewed_refresh.mjs \
      --project ORIGINAL_PRIVATE_PROJECT \
      --source ORIGINAL_SOURCE_UUID \
      --previous-publication ORIGINAL_PUBLICATION_UUID \
      --after-capture ORIGINAL_AFTER_CAPTURE/capture.json \
      --out PRIVATE_OUTPUT \
      --received NEW_PRIVATE_RECEIVING_PROJECT \
      --keys _id \

For live acquisition, replace --after-capture with --after-selection. The
selection uses the original capture engine's catalogue resource, query,

edition ID are saved before its completion, so the same invocation resumes its

The program completes the full publisher workflow, iterates every change,
downloads the complete authenticated JSONL, receives the whole project,
reopens it through the real managed MCP host, exercises all seven refresh
tools, and reopens the accepted decision through the installed CLI. Its second
operator records keep-current followed by withdrawal of the old source in the
receiving copy. The accepted successor remains selected; both published
versions are queried again. It verifies that the original publisher enforces
that received source withdrawal.

The receiving journal retains exact source, capture, comparison, decision,
candidate and archive identities. The complete outputs include
accepted-refresh.ckanw and received-refresh-history.ckanw. The first contains
the original accepted publication; the second includes the subsequent
receiving operator's decisions. Process-local listener tokens stay in memory.

# Review CKAN meaning and deliver it to the customer

The CKAN workbench retains the source data dictionary and an explicitly selected
CSVW document with each captured edition. A reviewed field projection carries
that meaning into the original dataset publisher, portable merchant package,
SF82 seller and SF88 buyer request.

The source reader, CSV dataset engine, publisher journal and release store remain
the maintained implementations. This extension adds the binding between the
source's meaning and the particular columns delivered to a customer. It is
available through the [workbench](README.md), the existing
[merchant MCP workflow](MCP_WORKFLOW.md), and the
[publisher API](publisher/README.md).

## Capture the source dictionary with the data

Select the actual package and DataStore resource in the catalogue. Supply the
resource's explicit same-catalogue HTTPS `schemaUrl` when it has a CSVW schema.
The capture retains the first schema response in `schema.json` and the later
observation in `schema-after.json`, together with their source receipts and
SHA-256 identities. The manifest's `semanticSchema` selects the original schema
used for the edition. Its consistency record also reports a change observed
during capture.

The normal resource metadata and DataStore `fields[].info` remain part of the
retained source. Labels, notes and other meaningful dictionary entries can
supply a semantic document when the resource has no separate CSVW schema.
An edition containing neither a retained CSVW document nor meaningful field
metadata follows the ordinary dataset workflow.

Use the original source filter and pagination controls to capture the intended
population. Keep the original package, resource responses, page files and capture
manifest together when receiving an edition on another host. The schema
sidecars are part of the same capture and are copied into each publication plan.

## Review a useful public projection

The source has 12 physical fields and one virtual CSVW column. The following
mapping preserves the fields needed to identify and interpret a capacity
observation:

| Published alias | Source field | Physical value | Source meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observation_id` | `soda_hashbyte` | string | Declared source primary key and observation URI variable |
| `start_utc` | `start_time_utc` | string | `base#validFromDateTime`; source declares datetime |
| `zone` | `bidding_zone` | string | `emdo#hasBiddingZone`; bidding-zone code-list URI |
| `product` | `reserve_product` | string | `emdo#hasReserveProduct`; reserve-product code-list URI |
| `direction` | `reserve_direction` | string | `emdo#hasReserveDirection`; reserve-direction code-list URI |
| `price` | `price` | number | `base#priceValue`; unit comes from the separate price-unit field |
| `price_unit` | `price_unit` | string | `base#hasPricePerUnit`; units code-list URI |
| `capacity` | `volume` | number | `emdo#procuredCapacityValue` |
| `capacity_unit` | `volume_unit` | string | `base#hasPowerUnit`; units code-list URI |

The `base` and `emdo` prefixes above refer to
`https://data.svk.se/ontology/base` and
`https://data.svk.se/ontology/emdo`. The exact original URIs are retained in
`sourceDefinition`; each alias has its own `projectedDefinition`.

The original CSVW document declares `soda_hashbyte` as its primary key and uses
it in the table's observation `aboutUrl`. The projection therefore rewrites
that template to `{observation_id}`. The unit code-list template for
`volume_unit` becomes
`https://data.svk.se/ontology/codelist/units#{capacity_unit}`.
The virtual `_resource_type` column retains
`rdf:type → https://data.svk.se/ontology/emdo#CapacityMarketObservation`
in the CSVW document.

The source timestamps are retained with their original lexical form. The
published JSON scalar is a string, and the source's datetime declaration remains
available in its annotation. Select a separate explicit transformation when a
customer requires a different timestamp representation.

Keep price and capacity with their unit columns. In the retained reference the
unit values are `EUR-MW` and `MW`; their original code-list URIs provide the
machine-readable meanings. Native numeric encoding uses the source engine's
existing precision checks. Select `encoding: "text", type: "string"` when the
customer needs an exact numeric token that the native numeric contract cannot
represent. The resulting semantic document then records both the original
datatype and the published text representation.

The remaining physical fields are still retained in the source capture:
`start_time_sweden` is a separate local-time field, `soda_identity` is a
technical identifier, and `_id` is the DataStore internal ID. The original
CSVW schema marks `_id` with `suppressOutput: true`. Choosing a suppressed
field produces an explicit review issue.

An example reviewed projection is:

