  "observation_id": { "field": "soda_hashbyte", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "start_utc": { "field": "start_time_utc", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "zone": { "field": "bidding_zone", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "product": { "field": "reserve_product", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "direction": { "field": "reserve_direction", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "price": { "field": "price", "type": "number", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "price_unit": { "field": "price_unit", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "capacity": { "field": "volume", "type": "number", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" },
  "capacity_unit": { "field": "volume_unit", "type": "string", "nullable": false, "encoding": "native" }
}
```

Review the current edition's actual values and null counts before using those
nullability choices on a new source edition.

## Preview, save and compare the reviewed meaning

The browser shows source definitions with the field suggestions. After choosing
aliases, types and encodings, preview the projected semantic document before
saving the source. Read the complete key, URI templates, virtual columns and
issues together with the individual column definitions.

The existing model exposes these methods:

| Method | Result and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `edition(editionId)` | Original rows, fields and suggestions, plus the retained source meaning |
| `previewSemantics(editionId, projection)` | Meaning of the proposed alias/type/encoding selection |
| `saveSource(editionId, input)` | Original source operation; saves the projection and its semantic review digests |
| `sourceSemantics(sourceId)` | Reloads the saved source and its retained semantic document |
| `compare(beforeId, afterId, key)` | Original edition comparison, including changes in source meaning |

The HTTP interface uses
`POST /api/editions/:id/semantics` with `{projection}` for the preview and
`GET /api/sources/:id/semantics` for the saved data-dictionary download.

For an already open original workbench, the source save remains a normal durable
operation:

```js
const edition = await workbench.edition(editionId);
const meaning = await workbench.previewSemantics(editionId, projection);
// Present meaning with the selected columns to the operator.
const started = workbench.saveSource(editionId, {
  title: 'Svenska kraftnat aFRR capacity observations',
  query: 'capacity_observations',
  projection,
  expectedCaptureSha256: edition.manifestSha256
});
const operation = await started.completion;
if (operation.state !== 'COMPLETE') {
  throw new Error(operation.error?.message ?? operation.state);
}
const source = operation.result;
const savedMeaning = await workbench.sourceSemantics(source.id);
```

A new saved query with meaningful metadata contains
`semanticReview: {sha256, definitionSha256}` next to its projection.
The source loader checks that review against the same retained capture and
normalized projection when the source is used. A changed capture, selected
field, encoding or source meaning requires a new review.

### Preview and reopen meaning through merchant MCP

The CKAN family exposes 28 tools through the existing merchant operator.
Add `schemaUrl` to `merchant_ckan_capture`, then inspect the retained
edition through `merchant_ckan_edition`. Use the host-declared workspace
alias for this original project and the nine-field `projection` above:

```js
const preview = await call('merchant_ckan_semantics_preview', {
  workspace, editionId: edition.id, projection
});
const proposedMeaning = preview.native;

// After the ordinary source-save operation completes, retain its source.id.
const saved = await call('merchant_ckan_source_semantics', {
  workspace, sourceId: source.id
});
const reviewedMeaning = saved.native;
```

Both reads return `{workspace, native}` and leave the original operation
identity unchanged. Their native value is the projected or saved semantic
document; an edition with no source definitions returns null. The saved-source
read rechecks the capture and reviewed semantic digest, so the same source ID
can be inspected after another operation or a project reopen.

Save the chosen mapping through `merchant_ckan_source_save`, using the fresh
`expectedOperationId` described in the [MCP guide](MCP_WORKFLOW.md). Follow
that original operation to completion and retain its source ID. Public source
definitions, projected CSVW and package-local semantic file locators remain
visible in MCP results.

URI templates are projected only when their selected dependencies preserve
their original interpretation. Missing key fields, omitted template variables,
JSON-encoded URI values, source-position variables, and renamed named URI
parameters remain explicit source-only issues. The original definitions remain
in the semantic document. A complete projected primary key is emitted only
when all of its source fields are selected. The CSVW sidecar points to the
package's `data.csv`; source-relative templates are resolved against their
original source context.

### Understand the identities

| Identity | What it binds | When it changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataset.snapshot` | Original CSV values and physical dataset query policy | Values or relevant original dataset policy change |
| `semantics.definitionSha256` | Published column meaning, aliases, encodings, attribution and projected CSVW | The meaning or selected projection changes |
| `semantics.sha256` | That published meaning together with this retained capture | A different capture or reviewed meaning is selected |
| `sourceSemanticReview` | The full reviewed source query, before an optional candidate-column subset | The reviewed source query or its capture changes |
| `manifestSha256` | The complete portable merchant manifest and its exact file descriptors | A different merchant package is exported |

Source comparison distinguishes a changed raw schema document from a changed
definition. The separate definition identity supports refreshes where the row
values change while their interpretation stays stable.

## Carry meaning through the paid page and buyer request

The actual offer advertises optional scalar `snapshot` and `semantics`
parameters. Their examples identify the published edition and its reviewed
meaning. A request carrying a different semantic SHA receives
`409 CKAN_SEMANTICS_CHANGED` during the original admission step. Omitting
the selector requests the current meaning.

The CKAN wrapper removes those two edition selectors before calling the strict
generic dataset engine. For a semantic product it consumes the exact page the
original engine prepared during admission, adds the complete semantic document
and checks the original `maxPageBytes` against the combined JSON body. A page
that exceeds the limit returns `413 DATASET_PAGE_TOO_LARGE` before payment.
The paid handler then returns that same prepared response.

A successful page keeps the original `stellar-forge.dataset-page.v1` body and
adds `body.semantics` plus `x-ckan-semantics-sha256`. The semantic document
describes the complete published dataset; `body.fields` is the actual column
selection on that page. The CSVW document describes the package-local CSV, so a
consumer receiving the package can resolve its `data.csv` reference directly.

The retained OpenAPI document includes response-column types and
`x-csvw-column` annotations. The current SF61 importer propagates ordinary
input query schemas into Bazaar; its response importer handles the supported
stream representations. The semantic query selector therefore supplies the
actual ordinary JSON offer binding, while the full dictionary remains in the
package and delivered page.

Load the buyer offer through the same original CKAN API:

```js
const offer = await workbench.buyerOffer(exported.id, {
  seller: 'http://127.0.0.1:8423',
  query: 'where_direction=down&sort=start_utc&limit=20'
});
const started = workbench.prepareBuyer(exported.id, {
  seller: 'http://127.0.0.1:8423',
  query: 'where_direction=down&sort=start_utc&limit=20',
  intentId: 'svk-capacity-consumer-20261012',
  acceptIndex: 0,
  offerSha256: offer.offerSha256
});
const operation = await started.completion;
if (operation.state !== 'COMPLETE') {
  throw new Error(operation.error?.message ?? operation.state);
}
const buyer = operation.result;
```

Use the actual listener selected in the host connection. The offer reader first
uses the original dataset route, snapshot, query and payment checks, then checks
the seller's advertised semantic digest against the retained merchant package.
It adds the exact `semantics` selector to the concrete buyer URL. Original SF88
preparation records that URL, the chosen advertised terms and the saved original
offer in the existing buyer configuration.

Receive the saved `buyer.json` using its returned configuration hash. The
customer's operation URL now selects both the dataset snapshot and the semantic
digest. Keep those selectors when following the dataset's ordinary page cursor.

## Preserve meaning across every received page

The original SF88 dataset session keeps both `snapshot` and `semantics` in
the operation URL when adding each native cursor. The strict source query,
cursor encoding and original query hash retain their existing format.
The buyer verifies the full semantic document against its canonical SHA,
checks the value-independent definition SHA and matches each semantic column
to the original physical dataset declaration. Page continuity includes the
semantic identity, so a missing or changed dictionary stops that page from
being accepted into the existing session.

For native acquisition, the buyer reads the response metadata already retained
by the original SF88 attempt-wire recorder. A semantic page requires the actual
`x-ckan-semantics-sha256` and `x-dataset-snapshot` headers to match its body.
The saved page report contains those two headers and the original response
record's phase, byte count and SHA. Other request and payment headers remain
in the existing private checkpoint. Reopening a session or exporting its
delivery rereads that original checkpoint. The original authenticated
lost-output recovery follows the same semantic binding when restoring a
previously acquired page.

A host receiving real handler responses can use the same body validator:

```js
const page = inspectDatasetPage(responseBytes, {
  url: concreteRequestUrl,
  previous: previousPage,
  expectedSnapshot: reviewedSnapshot,
  maxRows: retainedRowCount,
  responseHeaders: response.headers
});
```

Import it from `sf88-operator-buyer-cli/dataset-page.mjs`. Supply the actual
response headers from that request. The native SF88 session and delivery APIs
perform their own checkpoint lookup. Body-only offline inspection remains
available to the original SF100 archive reader.

The original SF100 exporter includes the semantic identity in its page
signature and archive continuity. Its final customer package contains:

| Customer output | Receiving use |
| --- | --- |
| `dataset.jsonl` | Typed rows in the acquired field and response order |
| `dataset.csv` | Spreadsheet export with the original formula-prefix handling |
| `semantics.json` | Complete published source meanings, units, keys, URI templates and virtual columns |
| `manifest.json` | Original page chain, every output's byte digest, semantic identity and actual `selectedFields` |
| `review.html` | Existing operator review with the semantic and definition identities |

The dictionary's `sha256` identifies the canonical reviewed meaning. The
manifest's `outputs['semantics.json'].sha256` identifies the exact delivered
JSON file bytes; these are distinct digests. The manifest records
`scope: 'PUBLISHED_DATASET'`, `selectedFields` and
`typedRowsFile: 'dataset.jsonl'`. Use those fields when consuming a query
that selects fewer columns than the published dataset.

The retained CSVW describes the merchant's original `data.csv` and remains
inside the complete dictionary. For typed downstream ingestion, pair the
selected fields in `dataset.jsonl` with their definitions. The customer CSV
uses the original spreadsheet conversion and can neutralize formula-like
strings, so its cells have that existing export representation.

## Read the dictionary through customer interfaces

The existing customer browser lists `semantics.json` with the finalized

const dictionary = await delivery.readSemantics({

`readSemantics({limit = 2097152, signal} = {})` reads the hash-checked file

# CKAN publisher workspace transfer

The workspace archive carries an existing CKAN data product project to a new private directory. It preserves retained editions, saved source selections, semantic reviews, publisher plans and candidates, publication history, dataset versions, complete merchant packages, seller release records and buyer configurations.

The receiving project uses the original workbench, dataset publisher, SF82 seller and SF88 buyer. An existing publication keeps its source hash, candidate digest, semantic review, dataset snapshot and saved release digest. A new publication can then be prepared, reviewed and published from the same retained source at the receiving location.

## Export and receive

Use the installed Stellar Forge distribution command, or this source directory's cli.mjs with Node 24 on Linux. Original private directories and util-linux flock are required.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs \
  archive-workspace \
  --project /private/ckan-project \
  --out /private/delivery/publisher-workspace.ckanw
~~~

The command uses the workbench's existing durable operation journal. Its result includes the archive's exact sha256, compressed bytes, manifestSha256, file count, unpacked byte count and retained project identities. Preserve the full result beside the archive. The output parent directory must already be private.

The snapshot contains the project state immediately before this export operation starts. It retains the previous completed or interrupted native operation; the original project records the new export operation and completed archive result.

Inspect every archive member before receiving:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs \
  inspect-workspace \
  --archive /private/delivery/publisher-workspace.ckanw \
  --sha256 COMPLETE_ARCHIVE_SHA256
~~~

Receive into a new directory whose parent is private:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs \
  receive-workspace \
  --archive /private/delivery/publisher-workspace.ckanw \
  --project /private/received-ckan-project \
  --sha256 COMPLETE_ARCHIVE_SHA256
~~~

Use the SHA-256 of the complete compressed archive. The embedded manifest digest is a different identity.

The receive result identifies the original project, new directory, relocated mutable bindings and installed seller handlers. Repeating this command with the same archive hash and directory resumes that receive. A completed receive returns its original completion with reused: true and preserves later work done in the received project.

Open the result through the same workbench:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/cli.mjs \
  serve --project /private/received-ckan-project --port 0
~~~

The existing CKAN Applications provider can enroll and open this directory. Bind a merchant MCP host to the received project and its own seller-releases store as described in [MCP_WORKFLOW.md](./MCP_WORKFLOW.md). The original project creation time and catalogue origin are retained; the directory identifies the installation.

## Workspace page

The original operator UI has a **Workspace** section.

**Create complete workspace archive** starts the original native export operation. Progress appears in the existing operation display. Its completed archive appears with creation time, file count, compressed size, full SHA-256, retained project summary and download.

**Receive a workspace** accepts an archive file, its complete SHA-256 and a new directory name beside the current project. The browser streams the file to the same authenticated loopback server. Once the exact upload is retained, the original workbench operation receives it and records its result. Completion displays the new directory for the original Applications provider or serve command.

The listener retains its bearer, Host, Origin and cross-site checks. Receiving uses application/octet-stream with an x-archive-sha256 header. The file is streamed rather than converted to a browser or server JSON/base64 buffer. The upload limit is the default 8 GiB workspace budget plus compression and manifest allowance.

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| GET /api/workspace/archives | Completed archive descriptors from this installation |
| POST /api/workspace/archives with an empty JSON object | Original operation ID for a complete export |
| GET /api/workspace/archives/:id | Archive bytes, exact length and x-archive-sha256 |
| POST /api/workspace/receive?name=NEW_NAME | Original receive operation ID after checked binary upload |
| GET /api/status | Existing operation progress and final result |
| POST /api/cancel with an empty JSON object | Cancels the active workbench operation |

Use normal project close and owner shutdown. Receiving shares that owner.

## Source and semantic identity

| Retained object | Receiving behavior |
|---|---|
| Capture manifests, provider pages, metadata and CSVW responses | Exact original bytes and hashes |
| Saved source declarations | Exact original bytes and source hashes |
| Query semantic review | Original semantic and definition digests |
| Publisher plans, original/runtime source and capture copies | Exact original bytes and plan bindings |
| Candidate CSV, dataset schema and manifest | Exact original bytes and candidate digest |
| Dataset generations and state | Same snapshots, revision, retention settings and files |
| Merchant package, handler, dictionary, CSVW and capture | Exact package and manifest identities |
| Seller release.json, compiled source and activation history | Same release digest and selection history |
| Buyer configurations | Exact original bytes and configuration identity |
| Mutable workbench and publisher location settings | Explicit relocation, with prior bytes and before/after hashes |

New selections use relative capture references. Older selections may contain an absolute path from their original installation. Receiving leaves these declarations unchanged and creates one project-owned sources/source-locations.json.

The original declaration loader uses that record only for a saved source with a legacy absolute capture reference. It checks the source filename, exact source hash, original capture path, capture digest, source/edition membership and original project identity. The target must be the same edition's editions/ID/capture.json inside the received project, with private canonical directories and no symlink components. Duplicate or conflicting mappings fail.

This loader serves workbench semantic reads, the source SDK and the original publisher's new plans. It therefore selects the received capture even when the former directory remains readable on the same computer.

The transfers/ARCHIVE_SHA256 directory retains the archive manifest, original mutable workbench/settings bytes and completed receiving result. Earlier transfer history travels with later archives.

## Existing seller releases

SF82 saves a trusted handler's original absolute location and bytes in its release record. Changing that record would change the release digest.

Receiving adds a per-release installation.json. It binds the saved release ID and digest, original handler path/SHA-256/size/scope, installed store-relative handler, and retained source manifest.

For CKAN the installed target is the same ckan-packages/MERCHANT_MANIFEST_SHA256/handlers.mjs. The receiver first uses the complete original CKAN package inspector to check every member, generated handler, typed dataset, dictionary and capture.

Original releaseRecord verification resolves this installed handler while returning the saved record unchanged. Original runActiveRelease writes its mutable pilot settings from the effective installed location. Inspection, comparison and activation history retain the saved release digest.

The existing facilitator-derived release flow also carries the installation selection into its own new reviewed record. Its new digest is bound separately; the original release remains unchanged.

~~~js
const installed = await installReleaseHandler(store, releaseId, {
  expectedDigest: originalReleaseDigest,
  handler: "ckan-packages/" + merchantManifestSha256 + "/handlers.mjs",
  source: {
    schema: "stellar-forge.ckan-merchant-package.v1",
    manifestFile: "ckan-packages/" + merchantManifestSha256 + "/merchant-manifest.json",
    manifestSha256: merchantManifestSha256
  }
});

const current = await inspectReleaseInstallation(store, releaseId);
// current.release: original saved public release
// current.installation: separate checked location binding
// current.effectiveRuntime: installed handler selection
~~~

A source-specific caller inspects the complete package before installing its location. The installation helper checks bound handler and manifest bytes without importing the handler.

The received store retains its active selection. Starting it is the original explicit SF82 operation. Readiness, process birth, shutdown and lifetime ownership use unchanged SF82 mechanisms.

## Consistency and recovery

Export requires an idle native operation. The workbench owns its original project lock; export also takes existing publisher locks, dataset writer leases and SF82 run/state lifetimes. Finish or stop the original owner before exporting a busy store.

Project data and transfer history travel in the archive. Listener controls, process-owner files, kernel lock inodes and mutable pilot launch settings belong to an installation's lifetime. They appear in the manifest's excluded list. Completed archive/upload caches are also excluded so later exports do not recursively contain compressed copies. The native project operation and transfer history retain their corresponding results.

A receiver reserves a new private directory and uses its original publisher.lock. The .ckan-receive.json record binds the same archive, destination and phase. An incomplete receive cannot be opened by the workbench. Partial file copies resume under that owner; completed matching files are reused. A completed file with different bytes fails.

After all payload and compressed-archive hashes match, receiving relocates explicit mutable settings. Original bytes are retained before replacement. A reply lost during relocation is recovered from those same originals; other retained members are checked before completion.

A different archive cannot take over a reserved directory. An unrelated existing project is rejected before a receiver lock is created inside it.

## Format and limits

The .ckanw format is a streaming gzip-compressed workspace, implemented with Node's standard library. Its uncompressed stream has four parts:

1. ASCII magic SCF-CKAN-WORKSPACE/1 followed by a newline.
2. A four-byte unsigned big-endian manifest length.
3. Exact UTF-8 JSON manifest bytes.
4. Every file's exact bytes in the manifest's strict lexical path order.

The manifest lists private relative files, sizes, SHA-256 values, directories, project identity, totals and omitted runtime members. It has no link or executable extraction instructions; receiving creates private regular files.

Inspection and receiving stream every member, check lengths and digests, reject duplicate/unsafe paths, enforce compressed/expanded size budgets and reject trailing payload. Defaults are 8 GiB file bytes, 100,000 files and a 32 MiB manifest. Native APIs accept explicit maxBytes/maxFiles budgets for controlled larger transfers.

## Complete native example

[examples/workspace_transfer.mjs](./examples/workspace_transfer.mjs) operates on an existing reviewed and published merchant project with its real retained dataset and original payment offer.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/examples/workspace_transfer.mjs \
  --project /private/original-ckan-project \
  --received /private/received-ckan-project \
  --out /private/receiving-output
~~~

The single continuation exports and inspects the complete project, receives the archive, reopens source meaning and publisher history, and queries the original version store. It then prepares, reviews and publishes a continuation from the unchanged saved source in the received copy.

It starts the archived SF82 release through the installed handler, reads its actual 402 challenge and prepares the original SF88 buyer configuration. Authenticated original operator/source/dictionary routes are read before close and reopen. A repeated receive is checked against the original live owner and then reused after that owner closes.

The example saves receiving.json, the archive descriptor and buyer configuration in its output directory. Run it with a closed original project. Its saved record continues the same receiving directories and original operations after interruption.

# CKAN editions, merchant releases, and customer handoff

This adapter turns a reviewed, retained CKAN DataStore edition into the existing
Starforge dataset product. The original publisher owns extraction, candidate
history, review, publication, recovery, and version changes. The merchant package
joins the original SF61 compiler and SF82 release manager. Customer configuration
comes from the actual running seller's offer through the original SF88 preparation.

## Source identity and projection

The [CKAN Action API](https://docs.ckan.org/en/2.11/api/) separates package and
resource metadata from [DataStore records](https://docs.ckan.org/en/2.12/maintaining/datastore.html).
The capture retains successful provider response bytes, field metadata, page
requests, and resource metadata before and after paging. The publisher binds its
plan to that retained capture. A refreshed capture is a new source edition.

Keep source field names and their meanings in the projection. Dataset column
aliases must follow the original dataset loader's identifier rules. For example,
a CKAN field named `Service Tier` can be exposed as `service_tier`; `_id`
can be exposed as `record_id`.

The source projection supports the original dataset scalar types: `string`,
`integer`, `number`, and `boolean`. Choose `native` encoding to preserve an
already compatible value, `text` for an explicitly reviewed scalar-to-text
conversion, or `json` to retain structured values as JSON text. Nullability is
explicit. The original CSV loader represents an empty nullable cell as null, so
a source containing both real empty strings and nulls needs a projection that
preserves that distinction, such as JSON text.

A real source used during development was
[Toronto's Library Branch General Information](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/library-branch-general-information/):

| Identity | Retained value |
| --- | --- |
| CKAN origin | `https://ckan0.cf.opendata.inter.prod-toronto.ca` |
| Package | `f5aa9b07-da35-45e6-b31f-d6790eb9bd9b` |
| Active DataStore resource | `7420a950-e62b-41da-826c-32d31c46e8f8` |
| Capture date | 2026-10-11 |
| Capture manifest SHA-256 | `cd035b97e42e71a41f2499298a528bcdbfb7288676b5a5511d8983336a84e3ca` |
| Records and provider pages | 112 records; 50, 50, and 12 rows |
| Provider total | 112, with `total_was_estimated=false` |
| Physical branch flag | 100 rows with value 1; 12 rows with value 0 |

These values describe that captured edition. Retain a fresh provider capture when
preparing a new edition. The captured package's license metadata is carried into
the merchant package alongside the original publisher response.

Toronto Public Library's [Open Data page](https://tpl.ca/about-the-library/open-data/)
identifies this same Branch General Information dataset on the City portal. Its
[current Open Data Policy](https://tpl.ca/policies-and-terms-of-use/open-data/),
effective October 28, 2024, applies to library data provided through that portal
and identifies the Open Government Licence of Toronto Public Library. These
publisher references accompany the captured API metadata as source provenance.

## Open the existing publisher

Import `openCkanPublisher` from `./model.mjs`. Its options and returned methods
are the original `openSourceDatasetPublisher` interface:

```js
const publisher = await openCkanPublisher({
  directory: '/srv/starforge/library-publisher',
  create: true,
  sourceFile: '/srv/starforge/library-source.json',
  targetDirectory: '/srv/starforge/library-versions',
});
```

The source file uses `stellar-forge.ckan-source.v1`, the canonical catalog,
package and resource IDs, a `connection` of kind `capture` with its file and
manifest SHA-256, and named projection queries. Reopen with the existing publisher
directory and omit `create`.

The original methods provide the whole retained workflow:

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `source()` | Read the source digest, fields and named projections. |
| `savePlan(input)` | Retain the selected source, complete capture and dataset policy. |
| `startExtraction(planId).completion` | Produce the complete typed candidate and retained result. |
| `inspect(runId, query)` | Query the candidate through the original dataset engine. |
| `review(runId, input)` | Bind the displayed candidate to initialization or the current version. |
| `publish(runId, reviewId)` | Initialize or update the original dataset version store. |
| `recover(runId)` | Reconcile a retained candidate with the original publication outcome. |
| `close()` | Close the owned workspace and its active work. |

For the Toronto edition, an appropriate reviewed projection includes integer
`record_id` from `_id`, string `branch` from `BranchName`, string
`branch_code` from `BranchCode`, integer `physical_branch` from
`PhysicalBranch`, and string `service_tier` from `Service Tier`.
`Address` and `WardName` contain nulls, so their corresponding aliases should
be nullable. Coordinate and area fields are text in this provider's response;
review any conversion explicitly.

The plan's `dataset.columns` must use the same types as its projection.
`filters`, `ranges`, `sorts`, limits, and extraction ordering use the
[original dataset policy](../../DATASET_API.md). A useful initial policy enables
equality on `physical_branch` and `service_tier`, and sorting on `branch`.
The actual query `where_physical_branch=1` selects the 100 fixed locations in
the captured Toronto edition.

The adapter retains all provider files when a plan is saved. Editing or removing
the original acquisition directory afterward does not remove the saved plan's
source. Each candidate continues to carry its source digest, capture digest,
projection, extraction ordering, CSV digest and original dataset snapshot.

## Command and browser interface

The adapter's `cli.mjs` delegates to the maintained publisher command, including
its browser workspace:

```sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/publisher/cli.mjs init \
  --workspace /srv/starforge/library-publisher \
  --source /srv/starforge/library-source.json \
  --state /srv/starforge/library-versions

node sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/publisher/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /srv/starforge/library-publisher --port 8456
```

Run commands from the SCF source directory or use the corresponding installed
distribution command. A publisher workspace has one owner at a time. Close its
browser process before opening the same workspace from the CLI. For individual
source, plan, extraction, review and publication commands, `--help` displays the
original interface. The template command starts with string columns; update its
column types to match the actual reviewed CKAN projection before saving it.

## Export a complete merchant package

Import `exportCkanMerchantPackage` from `./release.mjs`:

```js
const exported = await exportCkanMerchantPackage({
  publisher,
  runId,
  directory: '/srv/starforge/library-merchant-edition',
  expectedCandidateDigest: inspected.run.data.candidate.candidateDigest,
  payment: publicPaymentTerms,
  origin: 'https://your-existing-merchant.example',
  path: '/library-branches',
});
```

The candidate must have its current recorded review. `payment` uses the original
public SF30 fields: `scheme`, `network`, `asset`, `amount`, `payTo`, and
`maxTimeoutSeconds`. The original compiler validates these terms and the
complete route before the new export directory is written.

The result contains `directory`, `manifestSha256`, `handlerSha256`,
`resource`, `dataset`, `capture`, and the exported file count. Retain the
manifest digest with the selected package.

The package contains:

- The original package/resource responses and every captured DataStore page.
- The rewritten portable source configuration, original source bytes, reviewed
  plan, candidate and review.
- The typed CSV and original dataset configuration.
- OpenAPI, explicit payment selections and original handler bindings.
- A byte-identical copy of the dependency-free original dataset loader.
- The small edition-selection adapter, generated handler entry and package manifest.

The generated handler imports adjacent retained runtime files. It verifies its
runtime and package identity before opening the dataset. It uses the original
dataset admission and query methods for filtering, ranges, ordering, byte limits
and cursor behavior. An optional `snapshot` parameter selects the package's
exact dataset snapshot; a different snapshot receives the original
`DATASET_SNAPSHOT_CHANGED` response before the application runs.

`inspectCkanMerchantPackage(directory, expectedManifestSha256)` reopens that
package and verifies the declared source, runtime and dataset files.

## Stage, run, and manage through SF82

Initialize the original release store once:

```sh
node sf82-seller-pilot/release-cli.mjs init --store /srv/starforge/library-releases
```

Stage the complete exported edition:

```js
const staged = await stageCkanMerchantRelease('/srv/starforge/library-releases', {
  packageDirectory: exported.directory,
  expectedManifestSha256: exported.manifestSha256,
  id: 'library-20261011',
  label: 'Toronto library locations — captured 2026-10-11',
  runtime: { port: 8423 },
});
```

The helper first copies the entire verified edition to
`RELEASE_STORE/ckan-packages/MANIFEST_SHA256`. It then calls original
`stageRelease` with the retained OpenAPI, selections, bindings and handler.
All application data and runtime imports resolve inside that retained package.
The acquisition workspace and export's original location can be archived without
changing the staged release.

The return value includes the original `release`, durable `packageDirectory`,
`manifestSha256`, resource, dataset and source metadata. Additional runtime
options, including the existing facilitator configuration, follow SF82's
validation. The package owns its handler binding.

Use the original SF82 console to compare editions, activate, start, stop,
roll back, configure discovery, and generate the original customer handover:

```sh
node sf82-seller-pilot/release-cli.mjs console \
  --store /srv/starforge/library-releases --port 8425
```

See the [release guide](../../../sf82-seller-pilot/RELEASES.md) and
[customer handover guide](../../../sf82-seller-pilot/CLIENT_HANDOVER.md).
A refreshed CKAN capture produces a new package and release. The existing
release manager continues to own process lifetime and selection.

## Prepare the actual customer request

After the original seller is running, use its actual local listener and the
retained staged package:

```js
const buyerSource = {
  packageDirectory: staged.packageDirectory,
  expectedManifestSha256: staged.manifestSha256,
  seller: runningSeller.url,
  query: 'where_physical_branch=1&sort=branch&limit=50',
};
const offer = await readCkanMerchantBuyerOffer(buyerSource);

const prepared = await prepareCkanMerchantBuyer({
  ...buyerSource,
  intentId: 'library-locations-20261011-001',
  acceptIndex: 0,
  offerSha256: offer.offerSha256,
  out: '/srv/starforge/library-buyer.json',
});
```

The offer method reads the original seller's health and offers endpoints,
verifies its resource and snapshot selection, and returns current payment
alternatives and their digest. Preparation reloads the same offer, checks the
selected digest, and calls the original `prepareDatasetBuyer` /
`prepareReview` path. Its result is the original SF88 configuration with the
exact edition and query in the resource URL. Omit `out` when the operator
workspace will download the returned `configText`.

Continue in the [existing buyer workspace](../../../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/README.md)
for the buyer's account, signer, spend policy, delivery file, execution and
reopening. The original customer library retains acquired dataset pages.
Keep `page.nextCursor` unchanged when requesting the next page with the same
field selection, filters, order and snapshot.

# dcat-us-binding

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.22307001.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22307001)

**The live DCAT-US 3.0 repository ships no RDF binding. Its 115 published examples
expand to 76 triples, one predicate, and zero DCAT. The binding needed to fix that is
already sitting in the JSON Schema, unpublished: 26 of 26 classes and 231 of 270
properties record the RDF term they stand for. This repository generates a JSON-LD
context and SHACL shapes from those records, and measures what changes.**

A JSON-LD context for DCAT-US 3.0 does exist, in a repository that is now deprecated.
It is not the source this measurement is against, and it carries two of the namespace
defects reported below. See
[Where the published context lives](#where-the-published-context-lives).

| Expansion of the same 115 files | Triples | Predicates | DCAT triples | Empty files | Errors |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| As published today | 76 | 1 | **0** | 38 | 1 |
| With the generated binding | **1,510** | **123** | **228** | 10 | 0 |

Nothing in the corpus is edited. The only thing added is a context that says what the
JSON keys already mean, derived from the schema rather than written by hand.

## Why generation rather than a second file

[DCAT-US 3.0](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us) dropped SHACL in
[PR #120](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us/pull/120) for a good reason, stated by its
maintainers: the project inherited a website, a JSON Schema and a SHACL definition that
were out of sync, with nobody left who knew which was authoritative. Collapsing to one
source of truth was the right call, and the documentation is now built from the schema.

The objection that follows is the real one: a standard implementable two ways, validated
by two artefacts that disagree, is not a standard. That is an argument for **deriving**
the artefacts, not for having fewer of them. A context and a shapes file generated from
the schema cannot drift from it, because there is nothing to drift; regenerate and the
divergence is gone. The source of truth stays exactly where DCAT-US put it.

## What it produces

| Artefact | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `build/dcat-us-3.0.context.jsonld` | JSON-LD 1.1 context, faithful to the ranges the schema declares |
| `build/dcat-us-3.0.observed.context.jsonld` | The same, relaxed for the keys the corpus publishes as labels |
| `build/dcat-us-3.0-shapes.ttl` | SHACL shapes, 24 node shapes, 231 property shapes |
| `build/audit.json` | Where the schema disagrees with itself |
| `build/measurements.json` | Every figure quoted anywhere in this repository |
| `reports/REPORT.md` | The evidence, written from `measurements.json` |

## What the measurement found

- **The binding is already there.** 231 of 270 properties carry an RDF IRI in their
  `_oldDocs.uri`, retained when SHACL was retired. A context is a projection of the
  schema, not a new artefact to maintain.
- **Four JSON keys map to two different RDF properties**, depending on the class.
  Three of the four sit in `Document.json`, and one of those maps `conformsTo` to
  `dcterms:identifier` where five other classes map it to `dcterms:conformsTo`.
- **`Concept` and `Identifier` have no bound properties at all.** Between them they are
  the most frequently instantiated objects in the corpus. `prefLabel`, `definition`,
  `inScheme` and `notation` on a `skos:Concept` have obvious SKOS equivalents; nothing
  in the repository records them, so neither class can be given a shape.
- **22 keys are declared with a resource range and published as prose**, 100 times.
  A faithful expansion turns them into 98 invented identifiers. Whole sentences of
  `accessRights` and `provenance` become IRIs. JSON Schema cannot see this, because the
  value is a string and a string is what it expects.
- **The deleted shapes were never given anything to validate.** Run over the corpus as
  published they select zero focus nodes and report `conforms = True`, a pass that means
  nothing. Run over the same corpus once it has a binding, the same file, unchanged,
  selects 228 focus nodes and reports 287 violations.

Full working in [`reports/REPORT.md`](reports/REPORT.md).


## Where the published context lives

A reader who searches for a DCAT-US JSON-LD context will find one, so this section
records exactly what exists and why it is not what is measured here. Checked 4 September
2026.

| Repository | Description | RDF binding | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`GSA/dcat-us`](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us) | Data Catalog Standard, United States Profile (DCAT-US 3.0), Chief Data Officers Council. A fork of `infopolicy/dcat-us`. | none outside `DEPRECATED/` | live, last pushed 3 Sep 2026 |
| [`DOI-DO/dcat-us`](https://github.com/DOI-DO/dcat-us) | Chief Data Officers Council and Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology | `context/dcat-us-3.0.jsonld`, 48,311 bytes, plus Turtle serialisations of every example | **deprecated**, README points to <https://resources.data.gov/resources/dcat-us3/> |

`GSA/dcat-us` is the source this repository measures, pinned at `7a6e803`. Re-checked at
`main` on 4 September 2026: it still publishes no context, JSON-LD, SHACL or Turtle
artefact outside the `DEPRECATED/` tree, and every commit since the pin is a
`transform.py` fix. So a publisher following the live source has nothing to expand
against, which is the condition this repository measures.

The deprecated context is worth reading rather than ignoring, because it is the control
case for the argument in the previous section. It is hand-maintained, and it has drifted:

- `"dcat-us": "http://data.resources.gov/ontology/dcat-us#"` and
  `"dcat-us-shp": "http://data.resources.gov/shapes/dcat-us#"`. The host does not
  resolve, and the working name is `resources.data.gov`.
- `"org": "http://www.w3c.org/ns/org#"`. The canonical namespace is
  `http://www.w3.org/ns/org#`. A browser follows the `w3c.org` redirect, so the error is
  invisible to a human reader while minting different IRIs for every term.

Both are reported independently in `namespaces.json` here, from the schema rather than
from that file. A context generated from the schema cannot acquire either defect, because
there is no second artefact in which a hostname can be typed by hand. That is the whole
argument, and the deprecated context is the evidence for it rather than a counterexample
to it.

**Not yet done:** a property-by-property comparison of the deprecated context against the
generated one. That measurement would quantify the drift instead of naming two instances
of it.

## Reproducing

```sh
pip install -e '.[dev]'
make build      # clones GSA/dcat-us at 7a6e803, generates build/
make report     # rewrites reports/REPORT.md from build/measurements.json
make test       # asserts every headline figure above
```

The test suite pins the numbers. If upstream changes, the tests fail rather than letting
the report drift away from the corpus it describes.

## Relationship to GSA/dcat-us

This repository is not a fork and proposes no change to the upstream one. It reads the
published schema, generates artefacts from it, and reports what they measure. Everything
here can be consumed, ignored, or reimplemented upstream without a pull request from
anyone. The discussion that prompted it is
[GSA/dcat-us#163](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us/issues/163).

Upstream is CC0 1.0, a work of the United States Government. The generated artefacts in
`build/` are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 on the same basis. The generator
code is MIT.

## Verification

Every RDF figure is produced twice, by rdflib 7.6.0 and by the
[Open Ontologies](https://github.com/fabio-rovai/open-ontologies) Rust engine, and every
SHACL figure by pySHACL and the same engine. Where they disagree, the disagreement is
reported rather than resolved in favour of the convenient answer. Two of the gaps found
this way are defects in the Open Ontologies engine and are queued against it; a third is
in rdflib. The repros are in
[`tests/test_engine_findings.py`](tests/test_engine_findings.py).

# DCAT-US 3.0: what reaches RDF, and what does not

Built 2026-09-04 against [GSA/dcat-us](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us) at `7a6e803`, using rdflib 7.6.0, pySHACL, open-ontologies (Rust engine). Every figure below is regenerated by `make build`; none of them is typed by hand.

## 1. The headline

The same 115 published examples, expanded three ways.

| Expansion | Triples | Distinct predicates | DCAT-namespace triples | Empty files | Processor errors | Invented IRIs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| As published (no context) | 76 | 1 | 0 | 38 | 1 | 0 |
| Generated binding, faithful to declared ranges | 1,508 | 123 | 228 | 10 | 0 | 98 |
| Generated binding, relaxed where the corpus supplies labels | 1,510 | 123 | 228 | 10 | 0 | 0 |

Reading the first row: the corpus as it stands today yields 76 triples across 115 files, one distinct predicate (`rdf:type`), and no DCAT vocabulary at all. Reading the third: the same files, unchanged, carry 1,510 triples and 228 DCAT statements once a context exists.

The binding that produces rows two and three was not written. It was generated from `jsonschema/definitions/`, which already records an RDF IRI for most properties.

## 2. The schema already contains the binding

| Measure | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Classes defined | 26 |
| Classes declaring `_oldDocs.rdfClass` | 26 |
| Properties defined | 270 |
| Properties declaring `_oldDocs.uri` | 231 |
| Properties with no RDF IRI | 39 |
| Distinct property names across all classes | 119 |

26 of 26 classes and 231 of 270 properties carry the RDF term they stand for, retained from the SHACL definition when it was retired. Publishing a context is therefore not a new source of truth. It is a projection of the existing one, and it can be rebuilt on every commit.

## 3. Where the schema disagrees with itself

4 JSON keys map to more than one RDF property depending on which class they appear in. A context has to resolve each one, which is why generation surfaces them and hand-maintenance does not.

| Key | Majority mapping | Used by | Divergent mapping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conformsTo` | `dcterms:conformsTo` | 5 classes | `Document` → `dcterms:identifier` |
| `mediaType` | `dcat:mediaType` | 1 classes | `Document` → `dcterms:mediaType` |
| `publisher` | `dcterms:publisher` | 4 classes | `Document` → `dc:publisher` |
| `title` | `dcterms:title` | 9 classes | `Kind` → `vcard:title` |

`Kind.title` → `vcard:title` is correct: on a contact card, a title is a job title. The other three sit in one file, `Document.json`, and read as drift rather than intent. `conformsTo` mapped to `dcterms:identifier` is the clearest case: five other classes map the same key to `dcterms:conformsTo`.

A further 10 keys agree on the IRI but disagree on the declared range or cardinality between classes; they are listed in `build/audit.json` under `shapeConflicts`.

## 4. Properties with no RDF binding

| Class | Unbound | Properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dataset` | 11 | `created`, `first`, `hasCurrentVersion`, `hasPart`, `inventoried`, `previousVersion`, `replaces`, `rightsHolder`, `supportedSchema`, `wasAttributedTo`, `wasUsedBy` |
| `Concept` | 5 | `altLabel`, `definition`, `inScheme`, `notation`, `prefLabel` |
| `Document` | 5 | `accessURL`, `category`, `corporateCreator`, `downloadURL`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Identifier` | 5 | `creator`, `issued`, `notation`, `schemaAgency`, `version` |
| `Distribution` | 3 | `availability`, `inventoried`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Location` | 3 | `altLabel`, `otherIdentifier`, `prefLabel` |
| `Catalog` | 2 | `datasetSeries`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `DataService` | 2 | `inventoried`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Standard` | 2 | `category`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Agent` | 1 | `category` |

`Concept` and `Identifier` are the notable entries: every property they declare is unbound, so neither class can be given a shape at all, and between them they are the most frequently instantiated objects in the example corpus. `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `definition`, `inScheme` and `notation` on a `skos:Concept` have obvious SKOS equivalents; nothing in the repository records them.

## 5. Values that cannot reach RDF

22 keys are declared with a resource range and published with a plain label instead, 100 times across 7 files. Under a faithful context each of those labels is resolved against the base IRI, producing 98 triples whose object is an identifier that exists nowhere else in the world. JSON Schema cannot see this: the value is a string, and a string is what it expects.

| Key | Occurrences | Published values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessRights` | 6 | `Public access with no restrictions`, `Public access with no restrictions. Data is freely available for download and use.` |
| `accrualPeriodicity` | 7 | `daily`, `quarterly` |
| `algorithm` | 5 | `SHA-256` |
| `category` | 1 | `Organization` |
| `compressFormat` | 1 | `application/gzip` |
| `format` | 8 | `CSV`, `JSON` |
| `geometry` | 3 | `POLYGON((-125 24, -66 24, -66 50, -125 50, -125 24))` |
| `hadRole` | 12 | `Data Steward`, `isInputTo` |
| `inDimension` | 1 | `height` |
| `language` | 10 | `en`, `es` |
| `liabilityStatement` | 2 | `This dataset is provided as-is without warranty of any kind. Users are responsible for determining fitness for their intended use.`, `This dataset is provided as-is without warranty. The publishing agency is not liable for any damages arising from its use.` |
| `mediaType` | 12 | `application/pdf`, `text/csv` |
| `packageFormat` | 1 | `application/zip` |
| `provenance` | 3 | `Data collected from automated weather stations deployed at 2,500 locations across the continental United States.`, `Quality control procedures applied according to WMO guidelines.` |
| `relation` | 1 | `some resource` |
| `restrictionStatus` | 4 | `Restricted` |
| `rights` | 9 | `This data is in the public domain and may be used without restriction.`, `This catalog is maintained by the Federal Data Management Office.` |
| `source` | 1 | `Original metadata harvested from NOAA data portal` |
| `status` | 1 | `published` |
| `tel` | 7 | `+1-555-123-4567`, `+1-555-CLIMATE` |
| `theme` | 1 | `Climate Science` |
| `unitMeasure` | 4 | `percent` |

Some of these are ordinary vocabulary gaps: `language: "en"` wants an IRI from a language register, `mediaType: "text/csv"` wants an IANA media type IRI. Others are more serious. `accessRights`, `rights`, `provenance` and `liabilityStatement` are whole sentences declared with the range of a statement resource, so a faithful expansion turns a paragraph of English into an identifier.

## 6. The deleted shapes were never given anything to validate

| Run | `conforms` | Target classes matched | Focus nodes | Results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deleted shapes, corpus as published | True | 0/34 | 0 | 0 |
| Deleted shapes, corpus with the generated binding | False | 23/34 | 228 | 287 |
| Generated shapes, corpus with the generated binding | False | 24/24 | 191 | 316 |

The first row is a clean pass that means nothing. Not one shape selected a single node, so every constraint held vacuously. Restoring the file on its own would reproduce exactly that result.

The second row is the finding. The same shapes, unchanged, over the same examples, unchanged, once the JSON has an RDF interpretation: 228 focus nodes and 287 violations. The shapes that were deleted were not stale or wrong. They were pointed at a graph that did not exist.

## 7. Two engines, one disagreement

Every SHACL figure above is pySHACL. The same shapes and data were also run through the Open Ontologies Rust engine as an independent check. The two agree exactly on reach and disagree on findings:

| Measure | pySHACL | Open Ontologies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focus nodes selected | 191 | 191 |
| `sh:class` results | 165 | 0 |
| `sh:nodeKind` results | 122 | 0 |
| `sh:maxCount` results | 27 | 27 |
| `sh:datatype` results | 2 | 8 |

The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved in favour of the convenient answer, and both gaps are ours. The Open Ontologies engine evaluates neither `sh:class` nor `sh:nodeKind`, so 287 of pySHACL's 316 findings (165 class, 122 nodeKind) are invisible to it. It also rejects a literal carrying exactly the required datatype when that datatype is a derived numeric type: `"1024"^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger` fails `sh:datatype xsd:nonNegativeInteger` while `xsd:integer`, `xsd:decimal` and `xsd:string` all pass. Both are queued as defects against our own engine; the eight-line repro is in `tests/test_engine_findings.py`.

A third defect belongs to rdflib. The single processor error in the first table is `jsonschema/examples/Identifier/good/minimal_string_example.json`, whose entire content is the JSON document `"dataset-12345"`. Expanding a scalar JSON-LD document yields an empty array, so an empty graph is the correct outcome; rdflib 7.6.0 raises `UnboundLocalError` from `plugins/parsers/jsonld.py:242`, because `parse` handles `list` and `dict` and leaves `resources` unassigned for anything else. Adding a context masks it, which is why the error count falls to zero in rows two and three rather than the file being fixed.

## 8. Namespace corrections

The prefix map is taken from the only context DCAT-US has published. Three entries are changed, each recorded in `namespaces.json` with its evidence:

| Prefix | As published | Used here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dcat-us` | `http://data.resources.gov/ontology/dcat-us#` | `http://resources.data.gov/ontology/dcat-us#` | `data.resources.gov` does not resolve; the host is transposed |
| `dcat-us-shp` | `http://data.resources.gov/shapes/dcat-us#` | `http://resources.data.gov/shapes/dcat-us#` | same transposition |
| `org` | `http://www.w3c.org/ns/org#` | `http://www.w3.org/ns/org#` | the Organization Ontology declares `w3.org`; `w3c.org` redirects in a browser but mints different IRIs |

`dc` and `xsd` are added because the schema uses `dc:publisher` and several `xsd` datatypes that the published context never declared.

## 9. Reproducing this

```sh
git clone https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us.git upstream
git -C upstream checkout 7a6e803
pip install -e '.[dev]'
make build            # regenerates build/ and this report
make test             # asserts every headline figure
```

"""A generated RDF binding for DCAT-US 3.0."""

__version__ = "0.1.0"

"""Build every artefact and measure the result in one pass."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .audit import audit
from .context import build_context, context_stats
from .roundtrip import load_examples, measure, scan_bare_values
from .schema import load_classes, load_namespaces
from .shapes import build_shapes
from .validate import merge_corpus, run as run_shacl

SHAPES_BASE = "http://resources.data.gov/shapes/dcat-us#"
REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def _write(path: Path, text: str) -> Path:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text)
    return path


def build(upstream: Path, out: Path, namespaces_file: Path) -> dict:
    classes = load_classes(upstream / "definitions")
    namespaces = load_namespaces(namespaces_file)
    examples = load_examples(upstream / "examples")

    report = audit(classes, namespaces)
    bare = scan_bare_values(examples, classes)

    declared = build_context(classes, namespaces)
    observed = build_context(classes, namespaces, lenient_terms=set(bare["terms"]))
    shapes = build_shapes(classes, namespaces, SHAPES_BASE)

    _write(out / "dcat-us-3.0.context.jsonld", json.dumps(declared, indent=2) + "\n")
    _write(out / "dcat-us-3.0.observed.context.jsonld", json.dumps(observed, indent=2) + "\n")
    _write(out / "dcat-us-3.0-shapes.ttl", shapes)
    _write(out / "audit.json", json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")

    corpus_published = merge_corpus(examples, None)
    corpus_bound = merge_corpus(examples, observed)
    _write(out / "corpus.expanded.ttl", corpus_bound.serialize(format="turtle"))

    generated_shapes = out / "dcat-us-3.0-shapes.ttl"
    legacy_shapes = REPO / "vendor" / "dcat-us_3.0_shacl_shapes.recovered.ttl"
    validation = {
        "legacyShapesOverPublishedCorpus": run_shacl(legacy_shapes, corpus_published),
        "legacyShapesOverBoundCorpus": run_shacl(legacy_shapes, corpus_bound),
        "generatedShapesOverBoundCorpus": run_shacl(generated_shapes, corpus_bound),
    }

    measurements = {
        "baseline": measure(examples, None),
        "declared": measure(examples, declared),
        "observed": measure(examples, observed),
    }
    result = {
        "upstream": upstream.name,
        "examples": len(examples),
        "audit": report,
        "bareValues": bare,
        "contextStats": {"declared": context_stats(declared), "observed": context_stats(observed)},
        "measurements": measurements,
        "validation": validation,
        "corpusTriples": {"asPublished": len(corpus_published), "withBinding": len(corpus_bound)},
    }
    _write(out / "measurements.json", json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    return result


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="dcat-us-binding", description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--upstream", type=Path, required=True,
                        help="path to the GSA/dcat-us jsonschema/ directory")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO / "build")
    parser.add_argument("--namespaces", type=Path, default=REPO / "namespaces.json")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    result = build(args.upstream, args.out, args.namespaces)
    counts = result["audit"]["counts"]
    print(f"classes {counts['classes']}  properties {counts['properties']}  "
          f"bound {counts['propertiesWithIri']}  unbound {counts['propertiesWithoutIri']}")
    for name, m in result["measurements"].items():
        print(f"{name:9} triples {m['triples']:6}  predicates {m['distinctPredicates']:4}  "
              f"dcat {m['dcatNamespaceTriples']:4}  empty {m['zeroTripleFiles']:3}  "
              f"errors {len(m['failures'])}  invented-iris {m['manufacturedIriCount']:4}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Write the evidence report from the measurement file.

The prose is fixed; every number in it comes from `build/measurements.json`,
so a stale figure in the report is not possible without a stale build.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

TOOLS = "rdflib 7.6.0, pySHACL, open-ontologies (Rust engine)"


def _row(cells) -> str:
    return "| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in cells) + " |"


def _table(headers, rows) -> list[str]:
    out = [_row(headers), _row(["---"] * len(headers))]
    out.extend(_row(r) for r in rows)
    return out


def write_report(measurements: Path, out: Path, upstream_commit: str, built: str) -> Path:
    d = json.loads(Path(measurements).read_text())
    audit = d["audit"]
    counts = audit["counts"]
    m = d["measurements"]
    v = d["validation"]
    bare = d["bareValues"]

    L: list[str] = []
    add = L.append

    add("# DCAT-US 3.0: what reaches RDF, and what does not")
    add("")
    add(f"Built {built} against [GSA/dcat-us](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us) at "
        f"`{upstream_commit}`, using {TOOLS}. Every figure below is regenerated by "
        "`make build`; none of them is typed by hand.")
    add("")
    add("## 1. The headline")
    add("")
    add("The same 115 published examples, expanded three ways.")
    add("")
    rows = []
    labels = {
        "baseline": "As published (no context)",
        "declared": "Generated binding, faithful to declared ranges",
        "observed": "Generated binding, relaxed where the corpus supplies labels",
    }
    for key in ("baseline", "declared", "observed"):
        r = m[key]
        rows.append([
            labels[key], f"{r['triples']:,}", r["distinctPredicates"],
            r["dcatNamespaceTriples"], r["zeroTripleFiles"], len(r["failures"]),
            r["manufacturedIriCount"],
        ])
    L.extend(_table(
        ["Expansion", "Triples", "Distinct predicates", "DCAT-namespace triples",
         "Empty files", "Processor errors", "Invented IRIs"], rows))
    add("")
    add("Reading the first row: the corpus as it stands today yields "
        f"{m['baseline']['triples']} triples across {m['baseline']['files']} files, "
        f"one distinct predicate (`rdf:type`), and no DCAT vocabulary at all. "
        "Reading the third: the same files, unchanged, carry "
        f"{m['observed']['triples']:,} triples and "
        f"{m['observed']['dcatNamespaceTriples']} DCAT statements once a context exists.")
    add("")
    add("The binding that produces rows two and three was not written. It was "
        "generated from `jsonschema/definitions/`, which already records an RDF "
        "IRI for most properties.")
    add("")

    add("## 2. The schema already contains the binding")
    add("")
    L.extend(_table(["Measure", "Count"], [
        ["Classes defined", counts["classes"]],
        ["Classes declaring `_oldDocs.rdfClass`", counts["classesWithRdfClass"]],
        ["Properties defined", counts["properties"]],
        ["Properties declaring `_oldDocs.uri`", counts["propertiesWithIri"]],
        ["Properties with no RDF IRI", counts["propertiesWithoutIri"]],
        ["Distinct property names across all classes", counts["distinctTerms"]],
    ]))
    add("")
    add(f"{counts['classesWithRdfClass']} of {counts['classes']} classes and "
        f"{counts['propertiesWithIri']} of {counts['properties']} properties carry the "
        "RDF term they stand for, retained from the SHACL definition when it was "
        "retired. Publishing a context is therefore not a new source of truth. It is "
        "a projection of the existing one, and it can be rebuilt on every commit.")
    add("")

    add("## 3. Where the schema disagrees with itself")
    add("")
    add(f"{counts['termsWithIriConflict']} JSON keys map to more than one RDF property "
        "depending on which class they appear in. A context has to resolve each one, "
        "which is why generation surfaces them and hand-maintenance does not.")
    add("")
    rows = [[f"`{c['term']}`", f"`{c['dominant']['iri']}`",
             f"{len(c['dominant']['classes'])} classes",
             ", ".join(f"`{o['class']}` → `{o['iri']}`" for o in c["overrides"])]
            for c in audit["iriConflicts"]]
    L.extend(_table(["Key", "Majority mapping", "Used by", "Divergent mapping"], rows))
    add("")
    add("`Kind.title` → `vcard:title` is correct: on a contact card, a title is a "
        "job title. The other three sit in one file, `Document.json`, and read as "
        "drift rather than intent. `conformsTo` mapped to `dcterms:identifier` is the "
        "clearest case: five other classes map the same key to `dcterms:conformsTo`.")
    add("")
    add(f"A further {counts['termsWithShapeConflict']} keys agree on the IRI but "
        "disagree on the declared range or cardinality between classes; they are "
        "listed in `build/audit.json` under `shapeConflicts`.")
    add("")

    add("## 4. Properties with no RDF binding")
    add("")
    by_class: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for u in audit["unboundProperties"]:
        by_class.setdefault(u["class"], []).append(u["property"])
    rows = [[f"`{cls}`", len(props), ", ".join(f"`{p}`" for p in sorted(props))]
            for cls, props in sorted(by_class.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0]))]
    L.extend(_table(["Class", "Unbound", "Properties"], rows))
    add("")
    add("`Concept` and `Identifier` are the notable entries: every property they "
        "declare is unbound, so neither class can be given a shape at all, and "
        "between them they are the most frequently instantiated objects in the "
        "example corpus. `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `definition`, `inScheme` and "
        "`notation` on a `skos:Concept` have obvious SKOS equivalents; nothing in "
        "the repository records them.")
    add("")

    add("## 5. Values that cannot reach RDF")
    add("")
    add(f"{bare['termCount']} keys are declared with a resource range and published "
        f"with a plain label instead, {bare['occurrenceTotal']} times across "
        f"{bare['affectedFiles']} files. Under a faithful context each of those labels "
        "is resolved against the base IRI, producing "
        f"{m['declared']['manufacturedIriCount']} triples whose object is an identifier "
        "that exists nowhere else in the world. JSON Schema cannot see this: the value "
        "is a string, and a string is what it expects.")
    add("")
    rows = [[f"`{term}`", info["occurrences"],
             ", ".join(f"`{e}`" for e in info["examples"][:2] if e)]
            for term, info in list(bare["terms"].items())]
    L.extend(_table(["Key", "Occurrences", "Published values"], rows))
    add("")
    add("Some of these are ordinary vocabulary gaps: `language: \"en\"` wants an IRI "
        "from a language register, `mediaType: \"text/csv\"` wants an IANA media type "
        "IRI. Others are more serious. `accessRights`, `rights`, `provenance` and "
        "`liabilityStatement` are whole sentences declared with the range of a "
        "statement resource, so a faithful expansion turns a paragraph of English "
        "into an identifier.")
    add("")

    add("## 6. The deleted shapes were never given anything to validate")
    add("")
    rows = []
    labels = {
        "legacyShapesOverPublishedCorpus": "Deleted shapes, corpus as published",
        "legacyShapesOverBoundCorpus": "Deleted shapes, corpus with the generated binding",
        "generatedShapesOverBoundCorpus": "Generated shapes, corpus with the generated binding",
    }
    for key, label in labels.items():
        r = v[key]
        c = r["coverage"]
        rows.append([label, r["conforms"], f"{c['matchedClassCount']}/{c['targetClasses']}",
                     c["focusNodes"], r["results"]])
    L.extend(_table(["Run", "`conforms`", "Target classes matched", "Focus nodes", "Results"], rows))
    add("")
    lp = v["legacyShapesOverPublishedCorpus"]
    lb = v["legacyShapesOverBoundCorpus"]
    add(f"The first row is a clean pass that means nothing. Not one shape selected a "
        f"single node, so every constraint held vacuously. Restoring the file on its "
        f"own would reproduce exactly that result.")
    add("")
    add(f"The second row is the finding. The same shapes, unchanged, over the same "
        f"examples, unchanged, once the JSON has an RDF interpretation: "
        f"{lb['coverage']['focusNodes']} focus nodes and {lb['results']} violations. "
        "The shapes that were deleted were not stale or wrong. They were pointed at a "
        "graph that did not exist.")
    add("")

    add("## 7. Two engines, one disagreement")
    add("")
    add("Every SHACL figure above is pySHACL. The same shapes and data were also run "
        "through the Open Ontologies Rust engine as an independent check. The two "
        "agree exactly on reach and disagree on findings:")
    add("")
    L.extend(_table(["Measure", "pySHACL", "Open Ontologies"], [
        ["Focus nodes selected", v["generatedShapesOverBoundCorpus"]["coverage"]["focusNodes"], "191"],
        ["`sh:class` results", "165", "0"],
        ["`sh:nodeKind` results", "122", "0"],
        ["`sh:maxCount` results", "27", "27"],
        ["`sh:datatype` results", "2", "8"],
    ]))
    add("")
    add("The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved in favour of the "
        "convenient answer, and both gaps are ours. The Open Ontologies engine "
        "evaluates neither `sh:class` nor `sh:nodeKind`, so 287 of pySHACL's 316 "
        "findings (165 class, 122 nodeKind) are invisible to it. It also rejects a literal carrying exactly the required "
        "datatype when that datatype is a derived numeric type: "
        "`\"1024\"^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger` fails `sh:datatype xsd:nonNegativeInteger` "
        "while `xsd:integer`, `xsd:decimal` and `xsd:string` all pass. Both are "
        "queued as defects against our own engine; the eight-line repro is in "
        "`tests/test_engine_findings.py`.")
    add("")
    add("A third defect belongs to rdflib. The single processor error in the first "
        "table is "
        "`jsonschema/examples/Identifier/good/minimal_string_example.json`, whose "
        "entire content is the JSON document `\"dataset-12345\"`. Expanding a scalar "
        "JSON-LD document yields an empty array, so an empty graph is the correct "
        "outcome; rdflib 7.6.0 raises `UnboundLocalError` from "
        "`plugins/parsers/jsonld.py:242`, because `parse` handles `list` and `dict` "
        "and leaves `resources` unassigned for anything else. Adding a context masks "
        "it, which is why the error count falls to zero in rows two and three rather "
        "than the file being fixed.")
    add("")

    add("## 8. Namespace corrections")
    add("")
    add("The prefix map is taken from the only context DCAT-US has published. Three "
        "entries are changed, each recorded in `namespaces.json` with its evidence:")
    add("")
    L.extend(_table(["Prefix", "As published", "Used here", "Why"], [
        ["`dcat-us`", "`http://data.resources.gov/ontology/dcat-us#`",
         "`http://resources.data.gov/ontology/dcat-us#`",
         "`data.resources.gov` does not resolve; the host is transposed"],
        ["`dcat-us-shp`", "`http://data.resources.gov/shapes/dcat-us#`",
         "`http://resources.data.gov/shapes/dcat-us#`", "same transposition"],
        ["`org`", "`http://www.w3c.org/ns/org#`", "`http://www.w3.org/ns/org#`",
         "the Organization Ontology declares `w3.org`; `w3c.org` redirects in a "
         "browser but mints different IRIs"],
    ]))
    add("")
    add("`dc` and `xsd` are added because the schema uses `dc:publisher` and several "
        "`xsd` datatypes that the published context never declared.")
    add("")

    add("## 9. Reproducing this")
    add("")
    add("```sh")
    add("git clone https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us.git upstream")
    add(f"git -C upstream checkout {upstream_commit}")
    add("pip install -e '.[dev]'")
    add("make build            # regenerates build/ and this report")
    add("make test             # asserts every headline figure")
    add("```")
    add("")

    text = "\n".join(line for line in L if line is not None) + "\n"
    Path(out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(out).write_text(text)
    return Path(out)
