# DCAT-US 3.0 JSON Schema

This directory contains JSON Schema definitions for validating DCAT-US 3.0 metadata.

## Structure

```
jsonschema/
├── definitions/                  # Individual schema definitions
│   ├── AccessRestriction.json
│   ├── Activity.json
│   ├── Address.json
│   ├── Agent.json
│   ├── Attribution.json
│   ├── Catalog.json
│   ├── CatalogRecord.json
│   ├── Checksum.json
│   ├── Concept.json
│   ├── ConceptScheme.json
│   ├── CUIRestriction.json
│   ├── DataService.json
│   ├── Dataset.json
│   ├── DatasetSeries.json
│   ├── Distribution.json
│   ├── Document.json
│   ├── Identifier.json
│   ├── Kind.json
│   ├── Location.json
│   ├── Metric.json
│   ├── Organization.json
│   ├── PeriodOfTime.json
│   ├── QualityMeasurement.json
│   ├── Relationship.json
│   ├── Standard.json
│   └── UseRestriction.json
├── examples/                     # Test examples organized by schema
│   └── {SchemaName}/
│       ├── good/                 # Valid examples (should pass validation)
│       └── bad/                  # Invalid examples (should fail validation)
├── docs/                         # Generated markdown documentation
├── doc_templates/                # Templates for documentation generation
├── test_json_schema.py          # Validation test script
├── generate_schema_docs.py      # Documentation generator
├── parse_old_docs.py            # Historical one-time DCAT-US HTML metadata import
├── check_missing_olddocs.py     # Check for missing _oldDocs sections
├── check_requirement_levels.py  # Check/fix requirementLevel values
├── check_undefined_fields.py    # Check for undefined fields in examples
├── create_null_examples.py      # Generate null-value test examples
├── pyproject.toml               # Python dependencies (Poetry)
└── package.json                 # Node.js dependencies (Prettier)
```

## Schema Definitions

The `definitions/` folder contains individual JSON Schema files for each DCAT-US class:

| Schema             | Description                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| AccessRestriction  | Access restriction information (NARA)           |
| Activity           | Provenance activity                             |
| Address            | Physical or mailing address                     |
| Agent              | Entity responsible for resources                |
| Attribution        | Attribution information                         |
| CatalogRecord      | Metadata about a catalog entry                  |
| Checksum           | Checksum for data integrity                     |
| Concept            | SKOS concept for controlled vocabularies        |
| ConceptScheme      | SKOS concept scheme                             |
| CUIRestriction     | Controlled Unclassified Information restriction |
| DataService        | API or service providing data access            |
| Dataset            | A dataset resource                              |
| DatasetSeries      | A series of related datasets                    |
| Distribution       | A specific representation of a dataset          |
| Document           | A document resource                             |
| Identifier         | Identifier with scheme information              |
| Kind               | Contact information (vCard)                     |
| Location           | Geographic location                             |
| Metric             | Quality metric definition                       |
| Organization       | An organization entity                          |
| PeriodOfTime       | Temporal coverage                               |
| QualityMeasurement | Quality measurement result                      |
| Relationship       | Relationship between resources                  |
| Standard           | A standard or specification                     |
| UseRestriction     | Use restriction information                     |

`definitions/Catalog.json` defines the catalog class and serves as the root catalog schema.

## Setup

### Prerequisites

This project uses [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/) for Python dependency management and Node.js for formatting tools.

**Python 3.13+** is required.

### Install Poetry

If Poetry is not already installed, use one of the following methods:

```bash
# Recommended
pipx install poetry

# Alternative installer from poetry.org
curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | python3 -
```

Verify installation:

```bash
poetry --version
```

### Configure Poetry Environment

From this `jsonschema/` directory:

```bash
# Ensure Poetry uses Python 3.13+
poetry env use python3.13

# Confirm selected interpreter and virtual environment
poetry env info
```

### Install Dependencies

```bash
# Install Python dependencies
poetry install

# Install Node.js dependencies (for Prettier)
npm ci
```

## Available Scripts

All repository scripts are listed below with a brief summary and usage.

### test_json_schema.py

Summary: Validates all `examples/{Class}/good` (must pass) and `examples/{Class}/bad` (must fail) against the schema registry.

```bash
poetry run python test_json_schema.py
```

### generate_schema_docs.py

Summary: Generates Markdown schema documentation in `docs/` from the JSON Schema files.

```bash
# Generate docs
poetry run python generate_schema_docs.py

# Check if generated docs are up to date (CI-friendly)
poetry run python generate_schema_docs.py --check

# Show CLI help
poetry run python generate_schema_docs.py --help
```

### parse_old_docs.py

Summary: Historical bootstrap script that imported `_oldDocs` metadata from the legacy DCAT-US HTML documentation.

Note: This was effectively a one-time import step. The imported metadata was manually corrected and refined in this repository afterward, so re-running the parser is not a meaningful validation step and its output should not be used as a test oracle.

For ongoing validation of `_oldDocs`, use:

- `poetry run python check_missing_olddocs.py`
- `poetry run python check_requirement_levels.py`
- `poetry run python check_example_coverage.py`

```bash
# Historical preview only
poetry run python parse_old_docs.py --dry-run --verbose

# Historical import/apply mode
poetry run python parse_old_docs.py

# Show CLI help
poetry run python parse_old_docs.py --help
```

### check_missing_olddocs.py

Summary: Reports schema properties missing `_oldDocs` metadata.

```bash
poetry run python check_missing_olddocs.py
```

Note: This script does not expose a dedicated `--help` interface; running it executes the check.

### check_requirement_levels.py

Summary: Compares top-level `requirementLevel` against schema `required` fields and optionally fixes mismatches. Falls back to legacy `_oldDocs.requirementLevel` if needed.

```bash
# Report mismatches
poetry run python check_requirement_levels.py

# Apply automatic fixes
poetry run python check_requirement_levels.py --fix

# Show CLI help
poetry run python check_requirement_levels.py --help
```

### check_undefined_fields.py

Summary: Verifies that example JSON files only use fields defined by their schema.

```bash
poetry run python check_undefined_fields.py
```

Note: This script does not expose a dedicated `--help` interface; running it executes the check.

### create_null_examples.py

Summary: Generates `null_example.json` files with required starter fields plus nullable optional fields.

```bash
poetry run python create_null_examples.py
```

Note: This script does not support `--help`; passing flags will still run generation logic.

### check_example_coverage.py

Summary: Checks whether good typical/complete examples include fields marked Mandatory or Recommended in top-level `requirementLevel`. Falls back to legacy `_oldDocs.requirementLevel` if needed.

```bash
# Coverage check
poetry run python check_example_coverage.py

# Verbose output
poetry run python check_example_coverage.py --verbose

# Show CLI help
poetry run python check_example_coverage.py --help
```

### add_schema_examples.py

Summary: Populates schema-level and property-level examples in `definitions/*.json` from `examples/{Class}/good/typical_example.json` and `examples/{Class}/good/complete_example.json`.

- Class-level `examples`: uses values from `typical_example.json`.
- Property-level `examples`: combines values from both typical and complete examples.
- `examples` arrays are rewritten from source files each run (idempotent and deterministic).

```bash
# Apply updates to schema definitions
poetry run python add_schema_examples.py

# Preview what would be updated without writing files
poetry run python add_schema_examples.py --dry-run
```

Typical workflow:

```bash
poetry run python add_schema_examples.py
npx prettier --write definitions/*.json
poetry run python generate_schema_docs.py
```

### convert_dcat_1_1_to_3_0.py

Summary: Takes a URL pointing to a valid DCAT-US v1.1 catalog and converts it to
a valid DCAT-US v3.0 catalog. Legacy v1.1 `isPartOf` string relationships are
converted into catalog-level `datasetSeries` entries, where the referenced
source dataset is promoted into a `DatasetSeries`, its dataset `identifier` is
mapped to the series `@id`, and its member datasets are removed from the top-level
`dataset` list. By default saves converted data to the
`converted_dcat_data` directory in this repository.

```bash
poetry run python convert_dcat_1_1_to_3_0.py --url="https://www.example.gov/data.json"
```

## Adding New Test Examples

To add test examples for a schema:

1. Create the directory structure under `examples/`:

   ```
   examples/{SchemaName}/good/
   examples/{SchemaName}/bad/
   ```

2. Add valid JSON examples to the `good/` folder. These should pass schema validation.

3. Add invalid JSON examples to the `bad/` folder. These should fail schema validation (e.g., missing required fields, wrong types).

### Example Structure

For the `Agent` schema:

```
examples/Agent/
├── good/
│   └── complete_example.json    # Valid Agent with all fields
└── bad/
    └── missing_required_name.json  # Missing required "name" field
```

### Naming Conventions

- Use descriptive names that indicate what the example tests
- For bad examples, name should indicate the validation issue (e.g., `missing_required_name.json`, `invalid_type.json`)

## Integration

### Validating Data Programmatically

The schemas use JSON Schema 2020-12 draft. Here's an example using Python:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from referencing import Registry, Resource

# Build a registry of all schema definitions
schema_dir = Path(".")
registry = Registry()

# Load Catalog schema
with open(schema_dir / "definitions" / "Catalog.json") as f:
    catalog_schema = json.load(f)
    registry = registry.with_resource(
        catalog_schema["$id"],
        Resource.from_contents(catalog_schema)
    )

# Load all definitions
for schema_file in (schema_dir / "definitions").glob("*.json"):
    with open(schema_file) as f:
        schema = json.load(f)
        registry = registry.with_resource(
            schema["$id"],
            Resource.from_contents(schema)
        )

# Create validator for Dataset
dataset_schema = json.load(open("definitions/Dataset.json"))
validator = Draft202012Validator(dataset_schema, registry=registry)

# Validate your data
data = {"@type": "Dataset", "title": "My Dataset", ...}
errors = list(validator.iter_errors(data))

if errors:
    for error in errors:
        print(f"Validation error: {error.message}")
else:
    print("Valid!")
```

See `test_json_schema.py` for a complete working example using the `jsonschema` and `referencing` libraries.

## Formatting

For consistency, we format all JSON schema files with [Prettier](https://prettier.io/). As a best practice, we check formatting in CI/CD and fail if files aren't formatted correctly.

Check formatting:

```bash
npx prettier --check definitions/*.json examples/
```

Apply formatting:

```bash
npx prettier --write definitions/*.json examples/
```

## Schema Metadata (\_oldDocs)

Each schema and property can include an `_oldDocs` object containing metadata extracted from the local DCAT-US HTML snapshot at `../DEPRECATED/docs/index.html`. This includes:

- `rdfClass` / `uri` - The RDF class or property URI
- `definition` - The formal definition
- `usageNote` - Usage guidance
- `rationale` - Rationale for inclusion
- `requirementLevel` - Mandatory/Recommended/Optional
- `range` - Expected value type

The repository originally seeded `_oldDocs` metadata from the legacy DCAT-US HTML documentation using `parse_old_docs.py`. That import was a one-time bootstrap step, and the resulting metadata has since been manually updated in places.

Because of that, `parse_old_docs.py` should not be treated as a regression test or as a source of truth for current schema metadata. A dry run is expected to report differences.

For current validation, use:

- `poetry run python check_missing_olddocs.py`
- `poetry run python check_requirement_levels.py`
- `poetry run python check_example_coverage.py`

If you need to inspect the historical importer behavior, you can still run:

```bash
poetry run python parse_old_docs.py
```

"""Dataset-level transformations from DCAT-US v1.1 to v3.0.

Each public function takes a dataset dict and returns a transformed copy when a
transformation applies.

Resources:
- https://resources.data.gov/resources/dcat-us3/
- https://resources.data.gov/resources/dcat-us-3-migration/
"""

import copy
import logging
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from dateutil import parser

from langcodes import Language, find, tag_is_valid


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

ACCESS_RIGHTS_BY_LEVEL = {
    "public": "public",
    "restricted public": "Access restricted. Contact the publisher to request access.",
    "non-public": "Not available for public release. Contact the publisher for more information.",
}

# There are four valid-but-unmapped values for `accrualPeriodicity`:
# asNeeded
# irregular
# notPlanned
# unknown
PERIODICITY_MAP = {
    "P1D": "daily",
    "P1W": "weekly",
    "P2W": "fortnightly",
    "P1M": "monthly",
    "P3M": "quarterly",
    "P6M": "biannually",
    "P1Y": "annually",
    "PT1S": "continual"
}


def propagate_license(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Copy dataset-level `license` down to each Distribution
    that does not already declare one.

    Does not remove the dataset-level `license`. Returns the dataset
    unchanged if there is no license on the dataset or no distributions
    to copy it to.
    """
    license_value = dataset.get("license")
    if not license_value:
        return dataset

    distributions = dataset.get("distribution")
    if not distributions:
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    for dist in new_dataset["distribution"]:
        if isinstance(dist, dict) and "license" not in dist:
            dist["license"] = license_value

    return new_dataset


def transform_access_rights(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Add `accessRights` based on the existing `accessLevel`.

    Does not remove `accessLevel`. Returns the dataset unchanged if
    `accessLevel` is missing or `accessRights` is already set.
    """

    if "accessRights" in dataset:
        return dataset

    access_level = dataset.get("accessLevel")
    if access_level not in ACCESS_RIGHTS_BY_LEVEL:
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    new_dataset["accessRights"] = ACCESS_RIGHTS_BY_LEVEL[access_level]
    return new_dataset


def transform_conforms_to(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `conformsTo` from a URI string to an array containing a
    Standard object, on both the Dataset and each nested Distribution.

    Per the DCAT-US v3.0 migration guide's "Additional improvements"
    section. Leaves values that are already arrays alone, and leaves
    objects (non-list, non-string) alone.
    """
    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    _upgrade_conforms_to(new_dataset)
    for distribution in new_dataset.get("distribution", []):
        _upgrade_conforms_to(distribution)
    return new_dataset


def transform_described_by(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `describedBy` from a URL string to a Distribution object,
    at both the Dataset level and on each nested Distribution.

    Folds `describedByType` (v1.1) into the new Distribution's `mediaType`.
    Per the DCAT-US v3.0 migration guide's "Additional improvements"
    section. Leaves `describedBy` alone where it is absent or already an
    object.
    """
    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    _upgrade_described_by(new_dataset)
    for distribution in new_dataset.get("distribution", []):
        _upgrade_described_by(distribution)
    return new_dataset


def transform_issued(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """DCAT-US v3.0 requires that `issued` be either 'date-time'
    or 'date'."""
    if "issued" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    value = dataset["issued"]

    # Pass through null and non-string values untouched; the schema
    # permits null, and anything non-str isn't ours to reinterpret.
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        # Not a valid ISO date/date-time (e.g. "2019") => unset it.
        del new_dataset["issued"]
        return new_dataset

    if parsed.time() == datetime.min.time():
        # Midnight => no meaningful time component, emit a plain 'date'.
        new_dataset["issued"] = parsed.date().isoformat()  # e.g. 2015-06-02
    else:
        # Normalize to UTC and format as a valid ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g. 2018-09-28T06:00:00Z).
        if parsed.tzinfo is None:
            parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        new_dataset["issued"] = parsed.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

    return new_dataset


def transform_landing_page(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `landingPage` from a URL string to a Document object
    with `title` and `accessURL`.

    The title is reused from the dataset's `title` field. Returns the
    dataset unchanged if `landingPage` is absent or not a string.
    """
    if "landingPage" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    value = dataset["landingPage"]
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    document = {"@type": "Document", "accessURL": value}
    if "title" in new_dataset:
        document["title"] = new_dataset["title"]
    new_dataset["landingPage"] = document
    return new_dataset


def transform_language(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Truncate RFC 5646 language tags to ISO 639-1 on the dataset and
    any nested distributions. A bare `language` string is wrapped in a
    list first so it still gets truncated. Non-string list entries are
    left alone."""
    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    if isinstance(new_dataset.get("language"), str):
        new_dataset["language"] = [new_dataset["language"]]
    _truncate_language(new_dataset)
    for distribution in new_dataset.get("distribution", []):
        _truncate_language(distribution)
    return new_dataset


def transform_modified(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    modified = dataset.get("modified")
    if not isinstance(modified, str):
        return dataset

    if _is_date(modified):
        new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
        new_dataset["modified"] = _to_valid_date(modified)
        return new_dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    duration = _as_duration(modified)
    mapped_duration = PERIODICITY_MAP.get(duration)
    if mapped_duration is None:
        new_dataset["accrualPeriodicity"] = "irregular"
    else:
        new_dataset["accrualPeriodicity"] = mapped_duration
    # `modified` is Recommended + nullable in DCAT-US v3.0
    del new_dataset["modified"]
    return new_dataset


def transform_rights(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `rights` from a single string to an array of strings.

    Per the DCAT-US v3.0 migration guide's "Additional improvements"
    section. Returns the dataset unchanged if `rights` is absent or
    already a list. Unsets `rights` if it is not a string or list.
    """
    if "rights" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    value = dataset["rights"]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        new_dataset["rights"] = [value]
    else:
        del new_dataset["rights"]
    return new_dataset


def transform_theme(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `theme` from a single string to an array.

    `theme` is `null` or an array of Concept in DCAT-US v3.0, with no
    bare-string form. Returns the dataset unchanged if `theme` is
    absent or already a list. Unsets `theme` if it is not a string or
    list.
    """
    if "theme" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    value = dataset["theme"]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        new_dataset["theme"] = [value]
    else:
        logger.warning(
            "Dataset %r has a `theme` of unexpected type %s; unsetting it.",
            dataset.get("identifier", "<unknown>"),
            type(value).__name__,
        )
        del new_dataset["theme"]
    return new_dataset


def transform_spatial(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `spatial` from a plain string or bbox string to a
    list of Location objects.

    Detects bbox format ("<minLon>,<minLat>,<maxLon>,<maxLat>") and emits
    a POLYGON WKT; otherwise treats the value as a prefLabel. Returns the
    dataset unchanged if `spatial` is absent.
    """
    if "spatial" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    value = dataset["spatial"]
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    bbox = _parse_bbox(value)
    if bbox is not None:
        new_dataset["spatial"] = [{
            "@type": "Location",
            "bbox": _bbox_to_polygon_wkt(bbox),
        }]
    else:
        new_dataset["spatial"] = [{
            "@type": "Location",
            "prefLabel": value,
        }]
    return new_dataset


def transform_sub_organization_of(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Wrap `publisher.subOrganizationOf` (and any nested chain of the
    same field) in arrays.

    In v1.1, `subOrganizationOf` is a single Organization object that
    can nest recursively. In v3.0, it must be an array of Organization
    objects (or null). Walks the chain and wraps each level.

    Returns the dataset unchanged if there is no publisher or no
    `subOrganizationOf` to wrap. Leaves values that are already arrays
    alone.
    """
    if "publisher" not in dataset:
        return dataset

    publisher = dataset["publisher"]
    if not isinstance(publisher, dict) or "subOrganizationOf" not in publisher:
        return dataset

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    _wrap_sub_organization_of(new_dataset["publisher"])
    return new_dataset


def transform_temporal(dataset: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert `temporal` from an ISO 8601 interval string to a list
    containing one PeriodOfTime. Whichever side(s) parse as a date
    become startDate/endDate; non-date sides (durations or anything
    else) are dropped. No-op if `temporal` isn't a string with one '/'
    or if neither side parses."""
    value = dataset.get("temporal")
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return dataset

    # Strip repeating interval prefix (e.g. "R/" or "R5/")
    if re.match(r'^R\d*/', value):
        value = re.sub(r'^R\d*/', '', value)

    if value.count("/") != 1:
        return dataset

    left, right = value.split("/")
    start = _as_date(left)
    end = _as_date(right)
    if start is None and end is None:
        return dataset

    period = {"@type": "PeriodOfTime"}
    if start is not None:
        period["startDate"] = start
    if end is not None:
        period["endDate"] = end

    new_dataset = copy.deepcopy(dataset)
    new_dataset["temporal"] = [period]
    return new_dataset


def _as_date(token: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the date portion of `token` if it (a) is a year, (b) is a year and month,
    or (c) parses as an ISO 8601 date or datetime, else None."""
    if len(token) == 4 and token.isdigit():
        return token

    if len(token) == 7 and token[4] == "-" and token[:4].isdigit() and token[5:].isdigit():
        return token

    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(token).date().isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _as_duration(value: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the bare ISO 8601 duration portion of `value` if it looks
    like a duration or a repeating interval (`R/<duration>` or
    `R<n>/<duration>`), else None."""
    if value.startswith("P"):
        return value
    if value.startswith("R"):
        _, _, rest = value.partition("/")
        if rest.startswith("P"):
            return rest
    return None


def _to_valid_date(value: str) -> str:
    """Return `value` unchanged if it's a Zulu date-time (ends with 'Z').
    Otherwise, truncate to the YYYY-MM-DD portion if possible."""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return value

    if value.endswith("Z"):
        return value

    # Datetime-ish string (e.g. "2022-01-01T00:00:00" or "2022-01-01 00:00:00") — take the date part.
    if ("T" in value or " " in value) and len(value) >= 10:
        return value[:10]

    return value


def _upgrade_described_by(obj: dict) -> None:
    """Upgrade `describedBy` in place from a URL string to a Distribution
    object, consuming `describedByType` (removed from `obj`, folded into
    the new Distribution's `mediaType`)."""
    if "describedBy" not in obj:
        return
    value = obj["describedBy"]
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return
    distribution = {"accessURL": value}
    if "describedByType" in obj:
        distribution["mediaType"] = obj.pop("describedByType")
    obj["describedBy"] = distribution


def _upgrade_conforms_to(obj: dict) -> None:
    """Upgrade `conformsTo` on `obj` in place from a URI string to an
    array containing a Standard object."""
    if "conformsTo" not in obj:
        return
    value = obj["conformsTo"]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return
    obj["conformsTo"] = [{"@type": "Standard", "identifier": value}]


def _wrap_sub_organization_of(organization: dict) -> None:
    """Recursively wrap `subOrganizationOf` in arrays, in place.

    Assumes `organization` is a v1.1-shaped Organization where
    `subOrganizationOf`, if present, is a single Organization object.
    Walks the chain and wraps each level.
    """
    if "subOrganizationOf" not in organization:
        return
    parent = organization["subOrganizationOf"]
    if isinstance(parent, list):
        # Already an array (recurse into each element in case any
        # element still has an unwrapped subOrganizationOf).
        for element in parent:
            if isinstance(element, dict):
                _wrap_sub_organization_of(element)
        return
    if not isinstance(parent, dict):
        return
    _wrap_sub_organization_of(parent)
    organization["subOrganizationOf"] = [parent]


def _parse_bbox(value: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float] | None:
    """Return (minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat) if `value` is a comma-
    separated bbox string, otherwise None.

    Note that a more complete implementation of this function is
    available here: https://github.com/GSA/datagov-harvester/blob/main/harvester/utils/general_utils.py#L885-L955
    """
    parts = [p.strip() for p in value.split(",")]
    if len(parts) != 4:
        return None
    try:
        nums = tuple(float(p) for p in parts)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return nums  # type: ignore[return-value]


def _bbox_to_polygon_wkt(bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> str:
    """Convert (minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat) to a closed POLYGON WKT
    string. The ring is traversed counter-clockwise and closes by
    repeating the first vertex."""
    min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat = bbox
    return (
        f"POLYGON(({min_lon} {min_lat}, "
        f"{max_lon} {min_lat}, "
        f"{max_lon} {max_lat}, "
        f"{min_lon} {max_lat}, "
        f"{min_lon} {min_lat}))"
    )


def _truncate_language(obj: dict) -> None:
    tags = obj.get("language")
    if not isinstance(tags, list):
        return

    normalized = []
    for tag in tags:
        if not isinstance(tag, str):
            continue
        try:
            lang = Language.get(tag) if tag_is_valid(tag) else find(tag)
        except LookupError:
            continue
        code = lang.language
        if code:
            normalized.append(code)

    obj["language"] = normalized


def _is_date(string):
    try:
        parser.parse(string)
        return True
    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
        return False

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the complete portable source package with an exact file manifest."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import zipfile

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
EXCLUDED={".git",".venv","node_modules","__pycache__","workspaces","delivery","output",".pytest_cache"}

def build(output,source_commit,dataset_result=None):
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-f0-9]{40}",source_commit):
        raise ValueError("Keep the complete original Git source commit.")
    output=Path(output).absolute()
    if ROOT==output or ROOT in output.parents:
        raise ValueError("Write the portable archive outside the source directory.")
    files=[]
    for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob("*")):
        relative=path.relative_to(ROOT)
        if any(part in EXCLUDED or part.startswith(".write-") for part in relative.parts):
            continue
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("A portable source package cannot contain symbolic links: "+str(relative))
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        if path.suffix in (".pyc",".csw",".sqlite3") or path.name.endswith(("-wal","-shm",".log")):
            raise ValueError("Move local runtime or workspace output outside the source tree: "+str(relative))
        body=path.read_bytes()
        files.append((str(relative),body))
    required={"run.py","semantic_operator/application.py","semantic_operator/rdf_engine.py",
              "ui/index.html","ui/app.js","ui/datasets.js","ui/style.css","reference/SOURCE-MANIFEST.json",
              "semantic_operator/dataset_engine.py","semantic_operator/dataset_application.py","DATASETS.md","DATASET_ENGINE.md",
              "README.md","OPERATING_GUIDE.md","NATIVE_ENGINE.md","RECEIVING.md","requirements.txt","examples/DATASET_RECEIVING.mjs"}
    if not required.issubset({name for name,_ in files}):
        raise ValueError("The complete operator source and guides are required.")
    source_map=dict(files)
    input_manifest_path="examples/dataset-inputs/receiving-inputs.json"
    if input_manifest_path not in source_map:
        raise ValueError("Include the complete original dataset receiving input manifest.")
    input_manifest=json.loads(source_map[input_manifest_path])
    if input_manifest.get("schema")!="commons-semantic-dataset-receiving-inputs/1":
        raise ValueError("The original dataset receiving manifest schema is required.")
    for item in input_manifest["files"]:
        target=(ROOT/"examples"/"dataset-inputs"/item["path"]).resolve()
        try:
            name=str(target.relative_to(ROOT))
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError("A receiving input lies outside the portable source closure.") from None
        body=source_map.get(name)
        if body is None or len(body)!=item["bytes"] or hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()!=item["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("A complete original receiving input is missing or changed: "+name)
    source_files=len(files)
    dataset_handoff=None
    if dataset_result:
        result_raw=Path(dataset_result).read_bytes()
        result=json.loads(result_raw)
        if (result.get("schema")!="commons-semantic-dataset-ui-receiving-result/1" or
                result.get("status")!="PASS" or result.get("closed") is not True):
            raise ValueError("Include only a completed, closed dataset receiving result.")
        handoff=result["final_handoff"]
        body=Path(handoff["path"]).read_bytes()
        if len(body)!=handoff["bytes"] or hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()!=handoff["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("The completed dataset handoff differs from its retained result.")
        from semantic_operator.security import unpack_files
        _,retained=unpack_files(body)
        if retained["metadata"].get("workspace_id")!=result["workspace_id"]:
            raise ValueError("The handoff belongs to a different received workspace.")
        files.extend([("receiving/Dataset-Workspace.zip",body),
                      ("receiving/DATASET-RESULT.json",result_raw)])
        guide=("Open the complete received dataset workspace\n"
               "============================================\n\n"
               "Start this package's original operator using README.md.\n"
               "In Receiving, import receiving/Dataset-Workspace.zip, then choose\n"
               "Open received operator. The complete source revisions, datasets,\n"
               "graph catalogues, native jobs, reports and decisions are retained.\n\n"
               "DATASET-RESULT.json records the completed internal public-reference\n"
               "operation. The authored development inputs are not customer data\n"
               "or a customer acceptance. See DATASETS.md for the operating flow.\n").encode()
        files.append(("receiving/START.txt",guide))
        dataset_handoff={"path":"receiving/Dataset-Workspace.zip",
                         "bytes":len(body),"sha256":handoff["sha256"],
                         "workspace_id":result["workspace_id"]}
    manifest={"schema":"commons-semantic-source-release/1","product":"Commons Semantic Interoperability Operator",
              "source_commit":source_commit,"files":[{"path":name,"bytes":len(body),
                "sha256":hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()} for name,body in files]}
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    temporary=output.with_name(output.name+".building")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary,"w",compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=9) as archive:
        for name,body in files+[("SOURCE-RELEASE.json",json.dumps(manifest,sort_keys=True,indent=2).encode()+b"\n")]:
            info=zipfile.ZipInfo("Commons-Semantic-Operator/"+name,(2026,10,12,0,0,0))
            info.compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            info.external_attr=(0o100644<<16)
            archive.writestr(info,body)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary) as archive:
        for item in manifest["files"]:
            body=archive.read("Commons-Semantic-Operator/"+item["path"])
            if len(body)!=item["bytes"] or hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()!=item["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("The packaged source differs from its complete manifest.")
    temporary.replace(output)
    body=output.read_bytes()
    return {"path":str(output),"bytes":len(body),"sha256":hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
            "source_commit":source_commit,"source_files":source_files,"included_files":len(files),
            "dataset_handoff":dataset_handoff}

if __name__=="__main__":
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output",required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--source-commit",required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-result",help="Optional completed DATASET-RESULT.json; include its exact final handoff.")
    args=parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(build(args.output,args.source_commit,args.dataset_result),indent=2))

# Working with named-graph datasets

The dataset workflow uses the same Sources, Mappings, Snapshots, Validation,
Queries, Changes, Jobs and Receiving views as the original graph workflow.
Saved graph jobs keep their version 1 contract. Dataset jobs use version 2 and
retain the complete graph catalogue alongside their canonical quad bytes.

## Retain and inspect the original source

In **Sources**, choose **TriG dataset** or **N-Quads dataset** and retain the
original file with its reference, edition and license. Local JSON-LD can also
be inspected as a dataset. **Inspect dataset** performs an original native job
and exposes the graph catalogue, including the default graph, named graphs,
quad counts and empty graphs. Open the completed job and preview its catalogue.

The public reference collection includes the unchanged W3C
`w3c/examples/conformance-standards.trig`. It has a default graph describing
quality and provenance and a named `https://dcat.example.org/testResult`
graph. These are public reference data, with their original source and license
in `reference/SOURCE-MANIFEST.json`.

N-Quads cannot encode the existence of an empty graph. When importing an
exported `dataset.nq`, attach its matching `graph-catalog.json` using
**Optional graph catalogue companion**. The source revision retains both
original artifacts. Their byte identities are checked together before the
native job reconstructs the dataset. An external N-Quads file without a
catalogue supplies only the graph membership represented in its bytes.

A TriG or JSON-LD source is parsed as one dataset, so a blank node shared
between graphs remains shared. Separate source documents retain separate
blank-node scope. A graph selector shown after inspection belongs to that
exact source edition.

## Build an explicit dataset snapshot

Select the original RDF data and CSV mapping revisions in **Snapshots**, then
set **Snapshot model** to **Dataset with named graphs**.

For each RDF source, select **All graphs** or choose individual graph
identities from its completed inspection. Sources without a completed dataset
inspection can still be included in full. Inspect them first when selecting
individual graphs.

For each CSV mapping, select a **Default graph** or enter a **Named graph IRI**
as its destination. This choice belongs to the snapshot; it does not revise
the original mapping or infer a graph name from table contents. Each generated
statement retains its source row, original lexical cell and mapping edition.

A completed dataset snapshot has these independent downloadable files:

| Artifact | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dataset.nq` | Complete canonical N-Quads, with graph membership |
| `dataset.trig` | A readable dataset serialization |
| `graph-catalog.json` | Every graph identity and empty-graph presence |
| `provenance.json` | Original source, source graph and mapped-row lineage |
| `report.html` | Native operation summary and selected source context |

Canonicalization uses **URDNA2015 implemented by PyLD 3.3.0**, with the declared
`commons-semantic-dataset-inventory/1` profile. When an empty graph has a blank
name, that identity participates in the same labeling operation through
collision-free temporary membership statements. The engine removes those
statements before emitting RDF. The catalogue records the profile with the
algorithm and implementation version, so another consumer can reproduce the
same labels from the complete dataset and catalogue.

The N-Quads SHA-256 describes the emitted quad bytes under that declared
profile. The dataset SHA-256 additionally binds the ordered graph inventory,
so an empty graph can change dataset identity without changing the N-Quads
bytes. Source provenance remains separate from semantic identity. Keep the
N-Quads and catalogue together when reproducing an identity that includes
empty blank graphs.

Canonical blank-node labels describe the structure of one snapshot. They do
not establish that a node in another edition is the same business entity.
Use stable source IRIs when that cross-edition identity is required.

## Validate a graph or a selected union

Choose the dataset snapshot and exact SHACL and ontology revisions in
**Validation**. The extra **Validation graph mode** controls whether the
engine validates each selected graph separately or creates an explicit union
of selected graphs for that run.

Per-graph validation can produce different results from validation of a
union: a required relationship may be in another graph. Select the intended
scope and inference mode as engineering inputs. The native worker constructs
the selected graph explicitly before calling pySHACL, avoiding an implicit
dataset-wide union.

The saved result retains the selected graph identities, findings, conformance
information, shape-source editions and full native reports. Invalid shapes
remain an explicit outcome. A review decision pins the exact validation
record, not the current source heads.

## Query the selected dataset view

In **Queries**, choose:

- **Retained default graph only**, or **Default plus selected named graphs**;
- all named graphs, or the exact named graphs available to `GRAPH`.

A default union joins the retained default graph with precisely the selected
named graphs. It does not add unselected graphs. `GRAPH` retains the selected
named-graph view.

For the bundled W3C dataset, a local query can inspect the named result graph:

```sparql
SELECT ?s ?p ?o
WHERE {
  GRAPH <https://dcat.example.org/testResult> { ?s ?p ?o }
}
ORDER BY ?s ?p ?o
```

SELECT results preserve URI, blank-node, literal, datatype, language and
unbound distinctions. The existing row limit remains explicit. FROM, SERVICE,
remote contexts and external imports cannot fetch unretained data. Dataset
catalogues remain authoritative for graph identity, including empty graphs;
a query result is an observation of its selected SPARQL view.

## Compare editions and review the change

Choose two dataset snapshots in **Changes**. Select graph scope, relationship
predicates, traversal depth and the impact node limit. **Impact traversal
scope** chooses relationships within each graph or across the selected union.

The complete comparison retains additions and removals as quads. Moving a
statement from one graph to another is a membership change even when its
subject, predicate and object stay the same. Graph inventory changes are
separate, so adding or removing an empty graph stays visible. The impact
limit applies to the traversal; it does not truncate the complete quad
difference.

A graph snapshot and a dataset snapshot have different models. Build two
snapshots in the same model before comparing them. Revise the original source
or mapping, build a new dataset snapshot, compare it to the previous one,
then record the decision against that exact comparison revision.

## Handoff, reopen and continue

Use the original **Receiving** handoff and encrypted **Recovery** workflows.
Dataset files, companion catalogues, source editions, pinned native jobs,
attempts, results and decisions travel with the same SQLite workspace and
content-addressed artifacts.

The receiving application understands graph job version 1 and dataset job
version 2. An older graph-only receiver rejects dataset jobs instead of
flattening them. Keep the complete current application and its pinned
dependencies with the handoff. The source packager includes both engines and
the native dataset controls.

The original worker owns cancellation and continuation. **Continue original**
uses the same pinned source bytes and scope, retaining earlier attempts. A
source correction is a new source revision and a new operation; it never
rewrites a completed job.

See [DATASET_ENGINE.md](DATASET_ENGINE.md) for the native parameter and artifact
contract, [OPERATING_GUIDE.md](OPERATING_GUIDE.md) for the shared controls and
[RECEIVING.md](RECEIVING.md) for the original completed graph receiving.

## Continue the dataset operation from its retained inputs

`examples/DATASET_RECEIVING.mjs` operates the original application using the
exact dataset input manifest from the engine operation. It requires an
existing Python environment with the pinned dependencies, an existing
Playwright module and an existing Chromium binary.

```sh
node examples/DATASET_RECEIVING.mjs \
  --workspace=/absolute/new-dataset-workspace \
  --operation=/absolute/dataset-operation \
  --inputs=/absolute/receiving-inputs.json \
  --python=/absolute/existing/python \
  --playwright=/absolute/existing/playwright-module \
  --chromium=/absolute/existing/chromium
```

The operation retains its step journal and exact original downloads outside
the workspace. Resume with the same arguments after an interruption. It
reads saved operation identities before submitting a command and continues
accepted native jobs through the original job controls.

Its journey includes the unchanged W3C source, explicit graph choices,
the separately labeled authored baseline and correction, SHACL in each
selected scope, cross-graph query results, full quad and graph-inventory
comparison, a source-bound internal review, complete handoff into a new
receiving parent, independent reopening of that received workspace, and
catalogue-preserving reuse of emitted N-Quads. The authored inputs are
development observations; they do not stand for SAIC data or acceptance.

`DATASET-STATE.json` records resumable progress. A completed
`DATASET-RESULT.json` names the actual received workspace, original file
hashes and complete handoffs. It is only marked closed after the original
host and browser have exited.

To deliver the complete source together with that finished workspace, pass
the completed result to the existing release builder:

```sh
python BUILD_RELEASE.py --output=/absolute/Complete-Semantic-Operator.zip \
  --source-commit=FULL_PUBLISHED_COMMIT \
  --dataset-result=/absolute/dataset-operation/DATASET-RESULT.json
```

The builder verifies the original handoff hash, every original archive member
and its received workspace identity. The resulting package contains
`receiving/Dataset-Workspace.zip`, the exact result and `receiving/START.txt`
beside the full operator source. Omitting `--dataset-result` keeps the
source-only packaging workflow.

# Dataset engine contract

This module extends the existing retained-input semantic operator with explicit RDF dataset semantics. The operator workflow is documented in [DATASETS.md](DATASETS.md). This document specifies the deterministic engine, source boundaries, artifact identities, query and validation scopes, and the meaningful source operation.

The original graph-mode job schema and graph artifacts remain supported by the original engine. Dataset jobs select their data model explicitly. They never silently flatten named graphs into an ordinary graph.

## Native implementation and source boundary

The dataset module uses RDFLib **7.6.0** for TriG, N-Quads, Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, local JSON-LD, SPARQL parsing and evaluation; pySHACL **0.40.1** for SHACL; and PyLD **3.3.0** for **URDNA2015**. It reuses the original engine's CSV parser, reviewed mapping validation, literal-lexeme handling, graph parsers, query guard, query result serialization, and SHACL implementation. It does not provide a replacement RDF grammar, SPARQL evaluator, or SHACL validator.

Canonicalization metadata is:

    {
      "algorithm": "URDNA2015",
      "implementation": "PyLD",
      "version": "3.3.0",
      "profile": "commons-semantic-dataset-inventory/1"
    }

The inventory profile is described below. It is a declared Commons extension for complete graph inventory; it is not a claim to implement RDFC-1.0 or to produce unmodified URDNA2015 N-Quads when empty blank graph membership affects labeling.

Every input is an already retained, absolute local file, declared with a unique key, format, exact byte count and SHA-256. The module verifies all declared original bytes before an operation. It preserves source IDs, revision metadata and original bytes through the existing caller. Its only writes are files in the caller's fresh, owned result directory.

The original native scope disables network access while a job executes. JSON-LD contexts must be local inline values; remote contexts and imports are refused. RDF/XML external entities and DTDs stay disabled. OWL import statements remain data and do not authorize fetching an ontology. SHACL uses the original explicit inference profile, with advanced features, JavaScript and OWL imports disabled.

Primary implementation sources:

- [RDFLib 7.6.0 graph and Dataset API](https://rdflib.readthedocs.io/en/7.6.0/apidocs/rdflib.graph/)
- [Pinned TriG parser](https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/blob/7.6.0/rdflib/plugins/parsers/trig.py)
- [Pinned N-Quads parser](https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/blob/7.6.0/rdflib/plugins/parsers/nquads.py)
- [Pinned JSON-LD parser](https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/blob/7.6.0/rdflib/plugins/parsers/jsonld.py)
- [Pinned SPARQL evaluation](https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/blob/7.6.0/rdflib/plugins/sparql/evaluate.py)
- [Pinned SPARQL query context](https://github.com/RDFLib/rdflib/blob/7.6.0/rdflib/plugins/sparql/sparql.py)
- [PyLD 3.3.0 release](https://pypi.org/project/PyLD/3.3.0/)
- [Released URDNA2015 implementation](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/pyld/blob/3ac1987d9be3648c09b7c7e34865ce82d637e742/lib/pyld/canon.py)
- [pySHACL 0.40.1 release](https://pypi.org/project/pyshacl/0.40.1/)
- [Pinned pySHACL validator](https://github.com/RDFLib/pySHACL/blob/0.40.1/pyshacl/validator.py)

## Job and result envelopes

The callable is:

    execute(job, input_paths, output_dir) -> result

Dataset jobs use schema **commons-semantic-native-job/2** and parameters.data_model equal to **dataset**. The action remains one of inspect, snapshot, validate, query or compare. Each input entry uses the existing key, format, bytes, sha256 and optional source metadata fields. input_paths maps those keys to the actual original local files.

The result uses schema **commons-semantic-native-engine-result/2** and retains the existing action, summary, files and warnings structure. Each file descriptor has path, media_type, role and title. The existing worker hashes and adopts these files into the original Store.

The result captures the module's exact source bytes at import, including SHA-256 and Git blob identity. It also records the supporting original RDF engine source identity and the actual installed dependency versions. A pinned-version mismatch refuses execution.

### Graph selectors

A graph is selected by one of these exact objects:

    {"type": "default"}
    {"type": "uri", "value": "https://example.org/graph"}
    {"type": "bnode", "value": "c14n0"}

The blank-node value excludes the _: prefix. It must come from the retained whole-source inspection or snapshot catalogue. A label from another parser invocation, document or edition does not establish identity.

The URIs urn:x-rdflib:default and urn:commons:semantic:dataset-default are reserved only as native graph identifiers. An input naming a graph with either URI is rejected explicitly. Their appearance as ordinary RDF subject, predicate or object IRIs does not turn that term into the default graph.

### Formats

TriG, N-Quads and local JSON-LD can retain named graphs. The declared format names are trig, nquads and json-ld. Original turtle, nt and xml graph inputs enter the dataset's default graph. CSV and JSON inspection retain the original behavior; CSV becomes RDF only through an explicitly reviewed mapping.

Native parser hooks register empty TriG and JSON-LD graph declarations. N-Quads has no statement for an empty graph, so an external N-Quads file alone cannot supply that inventory. The engine reports this limitation. A retained N-Quads snapshot is paired with its graph catalogue.

Only RDF 1.1 subject, predicate, object and graph terms are accepted. Generalized predicates, quoted triples and other RDF-star/RDF 1.2 term extensions are outside this profile. Simple literals and explicit xsd:string denote the same RDF 1.1 value representation, and language tags use lower case for identity. Numeric typed lexical values are preserved; "050.0" is not rewritten to "50". Original source bytes preserve source spelling and syntax.

## Canonicalization and complete graph identity

Each original RDF document is parsed and canonicalized as a whole **before** graph selection. Blank nodes shared between that document's graphs remain one node. The source's entire blank-node map, including graph names, then receives a document scope derived from the declared input key, source ID, revision and original SHA. Different input documents are never joined merely because they use the same blank-node label.

Selected source quads and reviewed CSV output are merged and canonicalized as one dataset. Graph names participate in the same blank-node mapping as subjects and objects.

PyLD's pinned canonicalizer mutates its supplied RDF term dictionaries and treats its own canonical prefix specially. The module supplies copied dictionaries and first changes all input blank labels to a temporary namespace, including labels from previously canonical N-Quads. It verifies the native issuer map against the native serialized result.

### Empty blank graph labeling profile

Ordinary quad canonicalization cannot distinguish two quad-symmetric blank nodes when only one names an empty graph. Assigning empty graph inventory after quad labeling could therefore give isomorphic datasets different catalogue identities.

The inventory profile supplies an auxiliary statement for **each empty blank graph** to the same native URDNA2015 labeling problem. Its subject is that graph's blank node. Its predicate, object and graph are fresh internal IRIs, chosen deterministically to avoid every actual RDF IRI, graph IRI and literal datatype in the input. The URI family is urn:commons:semantic:empty-graph-inventory:N with suffixes :member, :Graph and :graph, using the first collision-free nonnegative N.

These statements are used only to determine the native blank-node labels. They are removed before every N-Quads, TriG, catalogue count, provenance record, query, validation and comparison. No auxiliary graph is added to the retained graph inventory. Isolated empty blank graph names are included by the same mechanism. No second canonicalization algorithm is implemented.

If no empty blank graph requires an auxiliary statement, the quad labeling is ordinary PyLD URDNA2015. Otherwise, emitted N-Quads use the declared inventory profile's labels. Consumers must use the recorded profile and catalogue to reproduce the complete dataset identity.

### Dataset digest

dataset.nq contains the complete sorted canonical quad bytes under the recorded profile. nquads_sha256 hashes those exact bytes.

dataset_sha256 hashes this exact byte concatenation:

    b"commons-semantic-dataset-identity/1\n"
    + canonical_nquads_bytes
    + b"\0"
    + json_bytes(ordered_graph_selectors)

json_bytes is the original engine's UTF-8 JSON encoding: ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False, followed by one newline. Graph selectors are ordered by their compact, sorted-key, Unicode JSON representation.

The ordered inventory always includes the default graph, even when empty. It also includes every selected named graph, including empty URI and blank graphs. Dataset identity excludes origins, input filenames, source revisions and other provenance metadata. Those are independently retained and hashed in their original artifacts.

Two artifacts with the same quad bytes can therefore have different dataset identities because their empty graph inventory differs. Conversely, a changed source filename or origin record does not change an otherwise identical semantic dataset.

### Catalogue and companion validation

graph-catalog.json uses schema **commons-semantic-graph-catalog/1** and contains data_model, canonicalization, dataset_sha256, nquads_sha256, quad_count and an ordered graphs array. Each graph row contains graph, quad_count, empty and origins. Inspection and snapshot rows retain input_key, original sha256, source_graph, source ID and revision where supplied.

A companion catalogue must match the exact selected N-Quads byte hash, parsed quad count, complete graph inventory, per-graph counts, empty flags, canonical graph order and dataset digest. Duplicate graph names, omitted represented membership, altered canonical bytes or a different profile are refused.

The catalogue can add only graphs that are absent from the N-Quads and have zero quads. It cannot invent a nonempty graph or reassign a source quad. Restoring or reusing a snapshot must retain the pair; the existing portable handoff includes both.

## Inspect and snapshot

Inspect parameters include input_key and optional source_catalogs, an object mapping the N-Quads source key to its declared JSON catalogue key.

RDF inspection writes dataset.nq, dataset.trig, graph-catalog.json, inspection.json and report.html. inspection.json uses **commons-semantic-dataset-inspection/1** and contains kind=rdf_dataset, the exact source entry, dataset and N-Quads hashes, graph and quad counts, complete graph rows, descriptive term statistics, and a limited typed quad preview. The statistics explicitly describe a union for descriptive counts only; they do not change query or validation scope.

Snapshot parameters are:

    {
      "data_model": "dataset",
      "data_keys": ["selected"],
      "source_graphs": {"selected": "all"},
      "source_catalogs": {},
      "mappings": []
    }

A source_graphs value may instead be a graph-selector list. An omitted entry means all. The selection must refer to graphs from that exact whole-source inspection. Selecting only named graphs still leaves the dataset's required empty default graph.

Reviewed CSV mappings keep their existing parser and field contract. Every dataset mapping additionally records destination_graph explicitly. The destination may be default or a named IRI, and is retained even if the CSV has no data rows. A blank graph name is not accepted as a CSV destination. Null handling uses only the entered null_values; values, identifiers, datatype and language declarations are not inferred.

Snapshot artifacts are:

| File | Role | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dataset.nq | dataset | Complete canonical quads under the recorded profile |
| dataset.trig | trig | Same RDF dataset, including explicit empty graph blocks |
| graph-catalog.json | graph_catalog | Complete canonical graph identities and counts |
| provenance.json | provenance | Complete quad, graph, input and CSV-row origins |
| report.html | report | Summary, selected sources and complete graph inventory |

Provenance uses **commons-semantic-dataset-provenance/1**. Each quad includes typed terms, graph selector, exact canonical N-Quads line and original origins. RDF origins bind the selected source SHA and whole-source canonical quad. CSV origins retain raw cells, logical and physical row locators, mapping edition, field rule, datatype, language and destination. Source selection and blank-node scope maps are explicit. This is source traceability, not verification that an imported source's assertions are true.

## Explicit SHACL scope

Validation parameters name dataset_key, catalog_key, shape_keys, ontology_keys, inference, allow_infos, allow_warnings and:

    {"validation_scope": {"mode": "per_graph", "graphs": [graph_selector]}}
    {"validation_scope": {"mode": "union", "graphs": [graph_selector, graph_selector]}}

graphs may be all. At least one selected graph is required.

For per_graph, the module builds one ordinary RDFLib Graph for each selected catalogue graph, including an empty selected graph. Each is validated independently. For union, it builds one ordinary Graph from exactly the selected graphs. It does **not** pass an RDFLib Dataset to pySHACL, whose pinned validator otherwise enables default_union.

Shape and ontology inputs use the original graph-only source parser and original reviewed composition. A shape dataset is not silently flattened. Explicit inference remains none, rdfs, owlrl or both. Invalid shape composition and native validation failure remain distinct from nonconforming data.

The module retains each original text/RDF/findings report under a target prefix and writes aggregate findings.json with schema **commons-semantic-dataset-findings/1**. Every finding has target_id, the exact validation scope, source dataset identity, native finding fields and relevant source quads with graph membership. Empty scopes cannot produce a vacuous compliance result. Overall conforms is null when data could not be assessed.

## Explicit SPARQL scope

Query parameters name dataset_key, catalog_key, query, row_limit and:

    {
      "query_scope": {
        "default_graph": "default",
        "named_graphs": "all"
      }
    }

default_graph is default or union. named_graphs is all or an explicit list of named URI/blank selectors; the default selector is not accepted there.

- default reads the retained default graph only for ordinary basic graph patterns.
- union copies the retained default graph and **only the selected named graphs** into an explicit query default graph.
- GRAPH sees only the selected named graphs. Empty selected named graphs remain registered.

The query Dataset has default_union=False. The original parsed query guard rejects FROM and SERVICE and allows SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE. No text rewrite adds a LIMIT, changes a GRAPH name or invents a graph selection.

A query-local guard around the pinned native evalGraph checks actual bound graph membership before delegating. This includes names supplied through VALUES. It prevents an empty pattern from matching a missing or excluded graph and prevents the native default sentinel from being exposed as a named graph. The original function is restored in finally; graph-mode jobs are unaffected.

RDFLib can return a blank graph name through a GRAPH variable. SPARQL GRAPH constants use IRIs; a query _:label is not a stable way to select that retained blank graph. Use the catalogue selection and a variable.

The original typed SELECT JSON/CSV, ASK and complete graph-result serializers are reused. SELECT observes at most row_limit plus one row to report truncation; when truncated the total remains unknown. CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE are ordinary graph results by their query semantics and are labeled accordingly. dataset-query-scope.json binds the exact scope, original dataset/catalogue sources and result model.

## Comparison and impact

Comparison requires before_dataset_key, before_catalog_key, after_dataset_key and after_catalog_key. Optional before_provenance_key and after_provenance_key select exact retained provenance. The parameters also record edge_predicates, depth, node_limit and:

    {
      "comparison_scope": {
        "graphs": "all",
        "impact_mode": "within_graph"
      }
    }

The graph list can select graphs present on either side, so a removed graph remains comparable. impact_mode is within_graph or union.

The complete selected canonical quad difference and complete graph-inventory changes are always retained. A moved statement is not hidden because its union triple remains present. A separate ground-membership report identifies definite membership changes for equal nonblank RDF triples in default/IRI-named graphs.

Canonical blank labels are local to a whole dataset. Changes can relabel connected nodes. Matching c14n text across editions does not establish business identity, and the canonical quad difference is not a minimum-edit or common-subgraph matching claim. The warning applies to blank graph names as well. A reviewed source identifier or explicit application mapping is needed for business identity.

Impact traversal preserves before/after sides separately, even for equal IRIs. within_graph remains inside each original graph. union allows traversal across the selected graphs within the same snapshot; every relationship still includes its actual graph and side. Traversal uses incoming and outgoing selected resource edges, plus uses of a visited predicate IRI. Empty graph changes are reported directly without inventing an RDF edge.

depth and node_limit bound impact only. Complete additions/removals and graph-inventory changes are not truncated by those limits. Unknown total impact remains null when limited. Provenance, when selected, is validated against the full dataset and catalogue and every typed quad before use.

Outputs include additions.nq, removals.nq, graph-changes.json, changes.jsonl, impact-relationships.jsonl, impact.json and report.html. Added/removed N-Quads keep their respective snapshot labels; they are change fragments, not independently canonicalized standalone snapshots.

## One meaningful source operation

[examples/dataset-inputs/receiving-inputs.json](examples/dataset-inputs/receiving-inputs.json) pins the exact shared inputs used by the deterministic operation and the native UI/receiving continuation. It names the unchanged previously shipped W3C conformance-standards.trig separately from the explicitly authored development derivation.

The authored pair has a measurement node shared across named graphs; an activity spanning default and named graphs; a blank graph name also used as an object; empty IRI and blank graphs; an exact decimal lexeme; and a corrected edition that changes a value, moves graph membership and renames an empty IRI graph. The shapes demonstrate a failing single-graph check and a conforming explicit selected union. Additional small authored files cover separate-document blank labels, inline JSON-LD, CSV destination mapping and the quad-symmetric empty-graph identity case.

Run the pure operation with an existing pinned runtime:

    python3 examples/DATASET_ENGINE_OPERATION.py --output /absolute/new-operation

Use --resume for its retained journal after an interruption. The script uses the same source files and original execute entry point, records actual results as it progresses, and starts no browser, provider, worker service or second Store. Expected assertions in the input manifest are not observed outcomes until the operation returns its actual result.

The full native continuation uses examples/DATASET_RECEIVING.mjs with the same input manifest and the original operator's source, snapshot, scope, review and receiving paths. Its actual saved receipts establish which parts completed; source publication alone does not imply that a run or external client acceptance occurred.

# Native semantic engine and receiving

The operator works with retained local source revisions. RDFLib 7.6.0 parses RDF,
evaluates SPARQL and compares graphs; pySHACL 0.40.1 performs SHACL validation.
The application supervises one job process, binds its original input hashes and
publishes the complete output manifest. The engine does not open a provider,
start a worker or modify the application's records.

The original graph jobs retain version 1 semantics. Version 2 dataset jobs
use the same application and worker, with explicit named-graph selection,
PyLD's URDNA2015 and a declared inventory profile for empty blank graphs.
[DATASETS.md](DATASETS.md) describes that operator workflow;
[DATASET_ENGINE.md](DATASET_ENGINE.md) defines its native contract.

## Original source workflow

1. Inspect the complete selected Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, CSV or JSON.
   CSV cells remain strings. Inspection lists the exact original header names and
   physical row ranges; it does not infer a schema or trim values.
2. Select graph sources and review each CSV mapping. A mapping names the original
   headers, subject template, classes, fields, datatypes, language and null values.
   Template substitutions are URI-encoded. An empty cell is null only when that
   exact value was declared null. Every emitted statement retains its source and
   mapping references, including the original row and raw field value.
3. Build a snapshot. graph.nt is the complete canonical N-Triples graph;
   graph.ttl is its lexical-preserving Turtle representation. provenance.json
   binds the exact graph SHA-256 and records all original statements, source
   revisions, mapped rows and the original-to-snapshot blank-node correspondence.
4. Select a snapshot, shape files and optional ontology files for validation.
   Inference is an explicit none, rdfs, owlrl or both choice. Native meta-SHACL
   runs on the selected shapes. An invalid or incomplete selected shape set returns its complete
   native meta-validation graph and findings with shapes_valid=false,
   data_validation_performed=false and conforms=null. The findings identify referenced definitions in other declared inputs, so the
   operator can explicitly complete the selected profile. Original bytes stay unchanged.
   The complete report graph, text and findings are retained when data is nonconforming. Nonconformance is a native result,
   not an invented customer requirement or a failed acquisition.
5. Query the selected snapshot with native SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT or DESCRIBE.
   SELECT retains typed SPARQL JSON and a CSV whose companion columns distinguish
   bound/unbound values, IRIs, literals, blank nodes, datatypes and language tags.
   A reviewed row limit never rewrites the original SPARQL query. If another row
   exists beyond the limit, the result explicitly states that its total is
   unknown. CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE retain their complete graph outputs.
6. Compare two exact snapshots. RDFLib's maintained graph_diff produces complete
   additions and removals. Impact follows the reviewed predicates in both
   directions, and follows uses of a changed/visited predicate IRI. It preserves
   source and CSV-row links when the matching original provenance was selected.
   Depth and node limits are explicit. A limited impact traversal does not
   truncate the complete native graph difference.

## RDF terms and graph identity

Literal strings, language tags and datatype IRIs remain distinct terms. Native
Turtle numeric recognition is retained; a small adapter prevents the subsequent
int/Decimal conversion from discarding the original numeric token. A process-local
constructor adapter preserves normalizedString/token lexical whitespace while
retaining RDFLib's parsed value and ill-typed flag. A native TurtleSerializer
subclass quotes literals using the maintained N-Triples literal helper, avoiding
the standard pretty-printer's boolean/decimal/double lexical rewriting.

RDFLib owns blank-node canonicalization. A thin hook records its resulting node
map; it does not replace the canonicalization algorithm. Independent input
documents receive distinct blank-node scopes before their graphs are merged.
Before/after impact uses separate blank-node scopes because canonical labels are
graph-specific. URI identifiers remain comparable across snapshots.

Explicit JSON-LD typed STRING @value forms preserve their RDF lexical strings.
JSON NUMBERS follow RDFLib's native JSON-to-RDF conversion after JSON decoding;
their original numeric spelling and precision remain in the original source
bytes. The tool does not claim those JSON tokens were RDF string lexical forms.

The version 1 native job contract described here accepts RDF graphs. Native JSON-LD graph
selection is intercepted to reject every named @graph, including an empty named
graph and aliases/scoped contexts. Plain default graphs are accepted. Version 2
dataset jobs use the separate [dataset engine](DATASET_ENGINE.md) with explicit
whole-dataset identity and graph scope. They are not flattened into this graph model.

## Local evaluation boundary

Every declared input is checked again against its original byte count and SHA-256.
JSON-LD consumes the same decoded object that was checked for remote contexts and
@import. RDF/XML uses RDFLib's original SAX reader with external entities disabled,
a rejecting entity resolver and a DTD rejection handler. All data, shapes and
ontologies reach native evaluation as already parsed Graph objects.

SPARQL is parsed by RDFLib before evaluation. Native DatasetClause and
ServiceGraphPattern nodes are rejected recursively, including escaped/nested
queries. Updates are not query forms. SHACL SPARQL texts pass the same native
syntax boundary; SHACL-JS and automatic OWL imports are disabled. An owl:imports
statement remains an ordinary original assertion, but no import is fetched.
An isolated-process audit guard also rejects attempted network requests.
